"""
Tests for Store.list with delete parameter, verifying the specification:
- False: only non-deleted items
- True: only soft-deleted items (with .del suffix)
"""

import pytest
from borgstore.store import Store, ItemInfo
from borgstore.constants import DEL_SUFFIX

from . import key, list_store_names, list_store_names_sorted
from .test_backends import get_posixfs_test_backend  # noqa
from .test_store import LEVELS_CONFIG, posixfs_store_created  # reuse fixture


def test_list_delete_false_only_non_deleted(posixfs_store_created):
    """deleted=False must yield only items that are not soft-deleted."""
    ns = "zero"
    k0, k1, k2 = key(0), key(1), key(2)
    with posixfs_store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k0}", b"v0")
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k1}", b"v1")
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k2}", b"v2")
        # soft-delete k1
        store.move(f"{ns}/{k1}", delete=True)

        names = list_store_names(store, ns, deleted=False)
        assert names == [k0, k2], f"Expected only non-deleted items, got {names}"


def test_list_delete_true_only_deleted(posixfs_store_created):
    """deleted=True must yield only soft-deleted items, with .del suffix."""
    ns = "zero"
    k0, k1, k2 = key(0), key(1), key(2)
    with posixfs_store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k0}", b"v0")
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k1}", b"v1")
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k2}", b"v2")
        store.move(f"{ns}/{k1}", delete=True)

        items = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))
        names = [item.name for item in items]
        # The deleted item should have .del suffix
        expected = [k1 + DEL_SUFFIX]
        assert names == expected, f"Expected only deleted items with suffix, got {names}"
        # Also verify that the ItemInfo has the correct name (with suffix)
        for item in items:
            assert item.name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX), f"Deleted item name missing suffix: {item.name}"


def test_list_delete_false_empty_after_all_deleted(posixfs_store_created):
    """When all items are soft-deleted, deleted=False yields nothing."""
    ns = "zero"
    k0, k1 = key(0), key(1)
    with posixfs_store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k0}", b"v0")
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k1}", b"v1")
        store.move(f"{ns}/{k0}", delete=True)
        store.move(f"{ns}/{k1}", delete=True)

        names = list_store_names(store, ns, deleted=False)
        assert names == [], f"Expected empty list, got {names}"


def test_list_delete_true_all_deleted(posixfs_store_created):
    """When all items are soft-deleted, deleted=True yields all with suffix."""
    ns = "zero"
    k0, k1 = key(0), key(1)
    with posixfs_store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k0}", b"v0")
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k1}", b"v1")
        store.move(f"{ns}/{k0}", delete=True)
        store.move(f"{ns}/{k1}", delete=True)

        items = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))
        names = sorted(item.name for item in items)
        expected = sorted([k0 + DEL_SUFFIX, k1 + DEL_SUFFIX])
        assert names == expected, f"Expected all deleted items with suffix, got {names}"


def test_list_no_overlap(posixfs_store_created):
    """Results of deleted=False and deleted=True must be disjoint."""
    ns = "zero"
    k0, k1, k2 = key(0), key(1), key(2)
    with posixfs_store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k0}", b"v0")
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k1}", b"v1")
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k2}", b"v2")
        store.move(f"{ns}/{k1}", delete=True)

        normal = set(list_store_names(store, ns, deleted=False))
        deleted = set(item.name for item in store.list(ns, deleted=True))
        assert normal.isdisjoint(deleted), f"Overlap between normal and deleted: {normal & deleted}"


def test_list_delete_default_is_false(posixfs_store_created):
    """Default value of deleted=False must behave as deleted=False."""
    ns = "zero"
    k0, k1 = key(0), key(1)
    with posixfs_store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k0}", b"v0")
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k1}", b"v1")
        store.move(f"{ns}/{k1}", delete=True)

        names_default = list_store_names(store, ns)  # no argument
        names_explicit = list_store_names(store, ns, deleted=False)
        assert names_default == names_explicit, "Default should be same as deleted=False"


def test_list_delete_true_keeps_suffix_for_distinguishability(posixfs_store_created):
    """Caller must be able to distinguish deleted from non-deleted by suffix."""
    ns = "zero"
    k0, k1 = key(0), key(1)
    with posixfs_store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k0}", b"v0")
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k1}", b"v1")
        store.move(f"{ns}/{k1}", delete=True)

        # deleted=True items must have .del suffix
        for item in store.list(ns, deleted=True):
            assert item.name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX), f"Deleted item lacks suffix: {item.name}"
        # deleted=False items must NOT have .del suffix
        for item in store.list(ns, deleted=False):
            assert not item.name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX), f"Non-deleted item has suffix: {item.name}"


def test_list_delete_with_nesting(posixfs_store_created):
    """Test with nested namespace (level 1) to ensure recursion works."""
    ns = "one"  # level 1 nesting
    k0, k1 = key(0), key(1)
    with posixfs_store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k0}", b"v0")
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k1}", b"v1")
        store.move(f"{ns}/{k1}", delete=True)

        normal = list_store_names(store, ns, deleted=False)
        assert normal == [k0], f"Expected only non-deleted, got {normal}"

        deleted_items = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))
        deleted_names = [item.name for item in deleted_items]
        assert deleted_names == [k1 + DEL_SUFFIX], f"Expected deleted with suffix, got {deleted_names}"


def test_list_delete_empty_namespace(posixfs_store_created):
    """Listing an empty namespace should return empty lists for both modes."""
    ns = "zero"
    with posixfs_store_created as store:
        # Ensure the namespace exists (it should already be created by the fixture,
        # but we guard against backend implementations that may not pre-create it).
        # We store and delete a dummy item to guarantee the namespace directory exists.
        dummy = "dummy"
        store.store(f"{ns}/{dummy}", b"")
        store.delete(f"{ns}/{dummy}")

        assert list_store_names(store, ns, deleted=False) == []
        assert list(store.list(ns, deleted=True)) == []


def test_list_delete_sorted(posixfs_store_created):
    """List results should remain sorted (backend.list returns sorted)."""
    ns = "zero"
    keys = [key(i) for i in range(10)]
    with posixfs_store_created as store:
        for k in keys:
            store.store(f"{ns}/{k}", b"v")
        # soft-delete some
        for k in keys[::2]:
            store.move(f"{ns}/{k}", delete=True)

        normal = list_store_names(store, ns, deleted=False)
        assert normal == sorted(normal), "deleted=False list not sorted"
        deleted = [item.name for item in store.list(ns, deleted=True)]
        assert deleted == sorted(deleted), "deleted=True list not sorted"


def test_list_delete_undelete_consistency(posixfs_store_created):
    """After undelete, item should appear in deleted=False and disappear from deleted=True."""
    ns = "zero"
    k0 = key(0)
    with posixfs_store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/{k0}", b"v0")
        store.move(f"{ns}/{k0}", delete=True)

        # before undelete
        assert list_store_names(store, ns, deleted=False) == []
        assert [item.name for item in store.list(ns, deleted=True)] == [k0 + DEL_SUFFIX]

        # undelete
        store.move(f"{ns}/{k0}", undelete=True)

        # after undelete
        assert list_store_names(store, ns, deleted=False) == [k0]
        assert list(store.list(ns, deleted=True)) == []

import io
import pytest
from csv2md.table import Table


class TestPipeEscaping:
    """Tests for escaping pipe characters in table cells (issue #...)."""

    def test_simple_pipe_in_cell(self):
        """A pipe in a cell should be escaped with a backslash."""
        cells = [['a', 'b'], ['c|d', 'e']]
        table = Table(cells)
        output = table.markdown()
        # Original cell lengths: 'c|d' length 3, 'e' length 1
        # Separator widths: 3 and 1
        expected = (
            "| a   | b |\n"
            "| --- | - |\n"
            "| c\\|d | e |"
        )
        assert output == expected

    def test_multiple_pipes(self):
        """Multiple pipes in a cell should all be escaped."""
        cells = [['x|y|z']]
        table = Table(cells)
        output = table.markdown()
        # Original cell length: 5
        expected = (
            "| x\\|y\\|z |\n"
            "| ----- |"
        )
        assert output == expected

    def test_pipe_at_start_and_end(self):
        """Pipes at the beginning or end of a cell should be escaped."""
        cells = [['|start', 'end|', '|both|']]
        table = Table(cells)
        output = table.markdown()
        # Original lengths: '|start'=6, 'end|'=4, '|both|'=6
        expected = (
            "| \\|start | end\\| | \\|both\\| |\n"
            "| ------ | ---- | ------ |"
        )
        assert output == expected

    def test_already_escaped_pipe(self):
        """A cell that already contains a backslash-escaped pipe should keep it as is.
        (The issue expects that `\|` in the CSV remains `\|` in the output.)"""
        cells = [['a', 'b'], ['c\\|d', 'e']]  # cell value is 'c\|d'
        table = Table(cells)
        output = table.markdown()
        # Original lengths: 'c\|d' length 4, 'e' length 1
        # The patch currently double-escapes, so this test will fail – that's the bug.
        expected = (
            "| a   | b |\n"
            "| --- | - |\n"
            "| c\\|d | e |"
        )
        assert output == expected

    def test_html_entity_pipe(self):
        """HTML entity | should be preserved unchanged."""
        cells = [['test|pipe']]
        table = Table(cells)
        output = table.markdown()
        # Original length: 14
        expected = (
            "| test|pipe |\n"
            "| -------------- |"
        )
        assert output == expected

    def test_no_pipe_unchanged(self):
        """Cells without pipes should remain unchanged."""
        cells = [['hello', 'world']]
        table = Table(cells)
        output = table.markdown()
        expected = (
            "| hello | world |\n"
            "| ----- | ----- |"
        )
        assert output == expected

    def test_pipe_in_header_row(self):
        """Pipes in header cells should also be escaped."""
        cells = [['col|1', 'col2'], ['val', 'val2']]
        table = Table(cells)
        output = table.markdown()
        # Original lengths: 'col|1'=5, 'col2'=4, 'val'=3, 'val2'=4
        expected = (
            "| col\\|1 | col2 |\n"
            "| ----- | ---- |\n"
            "| val   | val2 |"
        )
        assert output == expected

    def test_alignment_with_pipes(self):
        """Alignment options should work correctly with escaped pipes."""
        cells = [['a', 'b'], ['c|d', 'e']]
        table = Table(cells)
        output = table.markdown(center_aligned_columns=[0], right_aligned_columns=[1])
        # Original widths: col0=3, col1=1
        # Center: width 3 -> ':-:' (':' + '-'*1 + ':')
        # Right: width 1 -> ':' ('-'*0 + ':')  (pre-existing separator bug)
        expected = (
            "| a   | b |\n"
            "| :-: | : |\n"
            "| c\\|d | e |"
        )
        assert output == expected

    def test_no_header_row_with_pipes(self):
        """The no_header_row option should still escape pipes in the data rows."""
        cells = [['x|y', 'z']]
        table = Table(cells)
        output = table.markdown(no_header_row=True)
        # Default headers 'a','b' added; original lengths: 'x|y'=3, 'z'=1
        expected = (
            "| a   | b |\n"
            "| --- | - |\n"
            "| x\\|y | z |"
        )
        assert output == expected

    def test_escape_pipes_static_method(self):
        """Direct test of the _escape_pipes static method."""
        # Simple pipe
        assert Table._escape_pipes("a|b") == "a\\|b"
        # Already escaped pipe – should remain unchanged (not double-escaped)
        # The patch currently double-escapes, so this test will fail – that's the bug.
        assert Table._escape_pipes("a\\|b") == "a\\|b"
        # Multiple pipes
        assert Table._escape_pipes("x|y|z") == "x\\|y\\|z"
        # No pipe
        assert Table._escape_pipes("hello") == "hello"
        # HTML entity
        assert Table._escape_pipes("|") == "|"
        # Mixed: already escaped and new pipes
        assert Table._escape_pipes("a\\|b|c") == "a\\|b\\|c"
        # Empty string
        assert Table._escape_pipes("") == ""
        # Only backslash (no pipe)
        assert Table._escape_pipes("a\\b") == "a\\b"
        # Backslash at end
        assert Table._escape_pipes("a\\") == "a\\"

import numpy as np
import pytest
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingRegressor
from sklearn.linear_model import Lasso
from sklearn import datasets

from skore import cross_validate, CrossValidationReporter
from skore.item.cross_validation_aggregation_item import CrossValidationAggregationItem
from skore.item.cross_validation_item import CrossValidationItem


class TestCrossValidateMultipleScorers:
    """Test that skore.cross_validate works with multiple scoring metrics."""

    @pytest.fixture
    def regression_data(self):
        X, y = datasets.load_diabetes(return_X_y=True)
        X = X[:100]
        y = y[:100]
        return X, y

    @pytest.fixture
    def estimator(self):
        return Lasso()

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "scoring",
        [
            ["neg_mean_absolute_error", "r2", "explained_variance"],
            ("r2",),
            ("neg_mean_absolute_error", "r2"),
            ["r2"],
            "r2",
            None,
        ],
    )
    def test_cross_validate_with_scoring(
        self, in_memory_project, estimator, regression_data, scoring
    ):
        """cross_validate should not raise when scoring is a list or tuple."""
        X, y = regression_data
        reporter = cross_validate(
            estimator,
            X,
            y,
            cv=3,
            project=in_memory_project,
            scoring=scoring,
        )
        cv_results = reporter.cv_results
        assert "fit_time" in cv_results
        assert "score_time" in cv_results
        if scoring is not None:
            test_keys = [k for k in cv_results if k.startswith("test_")]
            assert len(test_keys) > 0

    def test_aggregation_with_multiple_metrics(self, in_memory_project, estimator, regression_data):
        """Storing two CrossValidationReporter results with multiple metrics should not fail aggregation."""
        X, y = regression_data
        scoring = ["neg_mean_absolute_error", "r2", "explained_variance"]

        reporter1 = CrossValidationReporter(estimator, X, y, cv=3, scoring=scoring)
        reporter2 = CrossValidationReporter(estimator, X, y, cv=3, scoring=scoring)

        in_memory_project.put("cv", reporter1)
        in_memory_project.put("cv", reporter2)

        items = in_memory_project.get_item_versions("cv")
        assert len(items) == 2
        agg_item = CrossValidationAggregationItem.factory(items)
        assert agg_item is not None

    def test_aggregation_with_tuple_scoring(self, in_memory_project, estimator, regression_data):
        """Storing two CrossValidationReporter results with tuple scoring should not fail."""
        X, y = regression_data
        scoring = ("r2",)

        reporter1 = CrossValidationReporter(estimator, X, y, cv=3, scoring=scoring)
        reporter2 = CrossValidationReporter(estimator, X, y, cv=3, scoring=scoring)

        in_memory_project.put("cv", reporter1)
        in_memory_project.put("cv", reporter2)

        items = in_memory_project.get_item_versions("cv")
        assert len(items) == 2
        agg_item = CrossValidationAggregationItem.factory(items)
        assert agg_item is not None

            HistGradientBoostingRegressor(),
            X,
            y,
            cv=3,
            project=in_memory_project,
            scoring=["neg_mean_absolute_error", "r2", "explained_variance"],
        )
        assert reporter is not None

    def test_cross_validate_with_tuple_single(self, in_memory_project):
        """Reproduce the tuple case from the issue."""
        X = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]).reshape(-1, 1)
        y = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])

        reporter = cross_validate(
            HistGradientBoostingRegressor(),
            X,
            y,
            cv=3,
            project=in_memory_project,
            scoring=("r2",),
        )
        assert reporter is not None

import pytest

from dishka import Provider, Scope, WithParents, provide_all, make_container


def test_provide_all_with_withparents_simple():
    """Test that provide_all works with WithParents for simple inheritance."""
    class A1: ...
    class A2(A1): ...
    class A3(A2): ...

    class MyProvider(Provider):
        scope = Scope.APP
        provides = provide_all(WithParents[A3])

    container = make_container(MyProvider())

    a3 = container.get(A3)
    a2 = container.get(A2)
    a1 = container.get(A1)

    assert isinstance(a3, A3)
    assert isinstance(a2, A2)
    assert isinstance(a1, A1)


def test_provide_all_with_withparents_protocol():
    """Test that provide_all works with WithParents involving a Protocol.

    This test exposes a bug in the patch: the patch creates separate factories
    for each type in WithParents, which tries to instantiate the Protocol
    directly. The correct behaviour should be to create an alias for the
    Protocol pointing to the concrete class.
    """
    from typing import Protocol

    class MyProtocol(Protocol):
        def process(self) -> str: ...

    class MyImpl(MyProtocol):
        def process(self) -> str:
            return "processed"

    class MyProvider(Provider):
        scope = Scope.APP
        provides = provide_all(WithParents[MyImpl])

    container = make_container(MyProvider())

    impl = container.get(MyImpl)
    # This should work, but the patch tries to instantiate MyProtocol directly
    protocol = container.get(MyProtocol)

    assert isinstance(impl, MyImpl)
    assert isinstance(protocol, MyProtocol)
    assert impl.process() == "processed"
    assert protocol.process() == "processed"


def test_provide_all_with_mixed_types():
    """Test that provide_all works with mix of WithParents and regular types."""
    class A1: ...
    class A2(A1): ...
    class A3(A2): ...

    class RegularClass: ...

    class MyProvider(Provider):
        scope = Scope.APP
        provides = provide_all(WithParents[A3], RegularClass)

    container = make_container(MyProvider())

    a3 = container.get(A3)
    a1 = container.get(A1)
    regular = container.get(RegularClass)

    assert isinstance(a3, A3)
    assert isinstance(a1, A1)
    assert isinstance(regular, RegularClass)


def test_provide_all_with_withparents_no_type_error_on_definition():
    """Ensure that the original TypeError is not raised when defining the provider.

    The issue reported a TypeError: Cannot use ProvideMultiple as a factory.
    This test verifies that the provider definition and container creation
    succeed without that error.
    """
    from typing import Protocol
    from abc import abstractmethod

    class MyProtocol(Protocol):
        @abstractmethod
        def __call__(self, data: bytes) -> bytes: ...

    class MyImpl(MyProtocol):
        def __call__(self, data: bytes) -> bytes:
            return data

    # This should not raise TypeError
    class MyProvider(Provider):
        scope = Scope.APP
        interactors = provide_all(WithParents[MyImpl])

    # Container creation should also not raise TypeError
    container = make_container(MyProvider())

    # The following lines expose that the patch does not correctly handle
    # Protocols: it tries to instantiate MyProtocol directly instead of
    # creating an alias.  We keep these assertions to document the bug.
    impl = container.get(MyImpl)
    protocol = container.get(MyProtocol)
    assert impl is protocol
    assert callable(protocol)


def test_provide_all_without_withparents_still_works():
    """Existing provide_all without WithParents must still work."""
    class A: ...
    class B: ...

    class MyProvider(Provider):
        scope = Scope.APP
        provides = provide_all(A, B)

    container = make_container(MyProvider())
    a = container.get(A)
    b = container.get(B)
    assert isinstance(a, A)
    assert isinstance(b, B)


def test_provide_all_with_withparents_multiple_classes():
    """Test provide_all with multiple WithParents entries."""
    class Base: ...
    class Derived(Base): ...
    class Other: ...

    class MyProvider(Provider):
        scope = Scope.APP
        provides = provide_all(WithParents[Derived], WithParents[Other])

    container = make_container(MyProvider())
    derived = container.get(Derived)
    base = container.get(Base)
    other = container.get(Other)
    assert isinstance(derived, Derived)
    assert isinstance(base, Base)
    assert isinstance(other, Other)

"""
Tests for Store.list with the delete parameter, as specified in the issue:

- False will only list not-deleted objects
- True will only list soft-deleted objects
"""

import pytest
from borgstore.store import Store, ItemInfo
from borgstore.constants import DEL_SUFFIX
from . import key, list_store_names, list_store_names_sorted
from .test_backends import get_posixfs_test_backend

LEVELS_CONFIG = {"zero/": [0], "one/": [1], "two/": [2]}


@pytest.fixture()
def posixfs_store_created(tmp_path):
    store = Store(backend=get_posixfs_test_backend(tmp_path), levels=LEVELS_CONFIG)
    store.create()
    try:
        yield store
    finally:
        store.destroy()


class TestListDeleted:
    """Test the Store.list method with the delete parameter."""

    def test_list_deleted_false_only_non_deleted(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """deleted=False should yield only items that are not soft-deleted."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/item1", b"data1")
            store.store(f"{ns}/item2", b"data2")
            store.move(f"{ns}/item1", delete=True)  # soft delete item1

            items = list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))
            names = [item.name for item in items]
            assert names == ["item2"], f"Expected only non-deleted items, got {names}"
            # also verify no .del suffix appears
            assert all(not name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX) for name in names)

    def test_list_deleted_true_only_deleted(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """deleted=True should yield only soft-deleted items, with .del suffix."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/item1", b"data1")
            store.store(f"{ns}/item2", b"data2")
            store.move(f"{ns}/item1", delete=True)  # soft delete item1

            items = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))
            names = [item.name for item in items]
            assert names == ["item1.del"], f"Expected only deleted items, got {names}"
            # verify .del suffix is present
            assert all(name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX) for name in names)

    def test_list_no_overlap(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """The two lists should be disjoint."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/a", b"1")
            store.store(f"{ns}/b", b"2")
            store.store(f"{ns}/c", b"3")
            store.move(f"{ns}/a", delete=True)
            store.move(f"{ns}/c", delete=True)

            normal = set(item.name for item in store.list(ns, deleted=False))
            deleted = set(item.name for item in store.list(ns, deleted=True))
            assert normal.isdisjoint(deleted), f"Overlap between normal {normal} and deleted {deleted}"

    def test_list_empty_store(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """Both modes should return empty lists when there are no items in the namespace."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            # Ensure the namespace directory exists by storing a dummy item and deleting it permanently
            store.store(f"{ns}/_dummy", b"")
            store.delete(f"{ns}/_dummy")
            # Now the namespace exists but is empty
            assert list(store.list(ns, deleted=False)) == []
            assert list(store.list(ns, deleted=True)) == []

    def test_list_all_deleted(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """When all items are soft-deleted, deleted=False returns empty, deleted=True returns all."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/x", b"1")
            store.store(f"{ns}/y", b"2")
            store.move(f"{ns}/x", delete=True)
            store.move(f"{ns}/y", delete=True)

            normal = list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))
            assert normal == [], f"Expected empty, got {normal}"

            deleted = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))
            names = sorted(item.name for item in deleted)
            assert names == ["x.del", "y.del"], f"Expected all deleted items, got {names}"

    def test_list_none_deleted(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """When no items are soft-deleted, deleted=True returns empty, deleted=False returns all."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/p", b"1")
            store.store(f"{ns}/q", b"2")

            normal = list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))
            names = sorted(item.name for item in normal)
            assert names == ["p", "q"], f"Expected all items, got {names}"

            deleted = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))
            assert deleted == [], f"Expected empty, got {deleted}"

    def test_list_with_nesting(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """Test with nesting level > 0 to ensure the fix works there too."""
        ns = "one"  # level 1 nesting
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/00000000", b"data0")
            store.store(f"{ns}/00000001", b"data1")
            store.move(f"{ns}/00000000", delete=True)

            normal = list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))
            normal_names = [item.name for item in normal]
            assert normal_names == ["00000001"], f"Expected only non-deleted, got {normal_names}"

            deleted = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))
            deleted_names = [item.name for item in deleted]
            assert deleted_names == ["00000000.del"], f"Expected only deleted, got {deleted_names}"

    def test_list_undelete_restores_normal(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """After undelete, the item should appear in deleted=False and disappear from deleted=True."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/item", b"data")
            store.move(f"{ns}/item", delete=True)

            # before undelete
            assert list(store.list(ns, deleted=False)) == []
            assert [i.name for i in store.list(ns, deleted=True)] == ["item.del"]

            # undelete
            store.move(f"{ns}/item", undelete=True)

            # after undelete
            assert [i.name for i in store.list(ns, deleted=False)] == ["item"]
            assert list(store.list(ns, deleted=True)) == []

"""Tests for the publish-lib command exit code fix."""

import argparse
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

import pytest
from craft_cli import CraftError

from charmcraft.application.commands.store import PublishLibCommand


@pytest.fixture
def publish_lib_command():
    """Return a PublishLibCommand instance with mocked services and app."""
    app_mock = MagicMock()
    app_mock.name = "charmcraft"
    app_mock.appdir = "/fake"
    store_mock = MagicMock()
    services_mock = MagicMock()
    services_mock.store = store_mock
    config = {
        "app": app_mock,
        "services": services_mock,
    }
    cmd = PublishLibCommand(config)
    return cmd


def _make_lib_data(api=1, patch=1):
    """Create a minimal mock Library object for testing."""
    lib = MagicMock()
    lib.api = api
    lib.patch = patch
    lib.lib_id = "test-lib-id"
    lib.charm_name = "test-charm"
    lib.lib_name = "test-lib"
    return lib


class TestPublishLibExitCode:
    """Tests for publish-lib exit code on failure."""

    def test_publish_lib_success(self, publish_lib_command):
        """No error when all libraries publish successfully."""
        lib_data = _make_lib_data()
        analysis = [(lib_data, None)]
        with patch.object(
            publish_lib_command, "_get_libs_data", return_value=analysis
        ):
            # Should not raise any exception
            publish_lib_command.run(argparse.Namespace(format=None))

    def test_publish_lib_failure_raises_craft_error(self, publish_lib_command):
        """CraftError is raised when a library fails to publish."""
        lib_data = _make_lib_data()
        error_message = "LIBPATCH is not bumped"
        analysis = [(lib_data, error_message)]
        with patch.object(
            publish_lib_command, "_get_libs_data", return_value=analysis
        ):

                publish_lib_command.run(argparse.Namespace(format=None))

        with patch.object(

"""Tests for the issue: daemon should delete suspect/corrupt files and CLI --include-bad option."""

import pytest
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock

from alpenhorn.db import (
    StorageGroup,
    StorageNode,
    ArchiveAcq,
    ArchiveFile,
    ArchiveFileCopy,
    ArchiveFileCopyRequest,
    utcnow,
)
from alpenhorn.daemon.update import UpdateableNode


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Daemon tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_update_delete_includes_bad(xfs, mockgroupandnode, queue):
    """update_delete should delete copies with has_file='X' or 'M' and wants_file='N'."""
    mockio, group, node = mockgroupandnode

    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")
    file_corrupt = ArchiveFile.create(name="corrupt", acq=acq, size_b=1000)
    file_suspect = ArchiveFile.create(name="suspect", acq=acq, size_b=1000)
    file_valid = ArchiveFile.create(name="valid", acq=acq, size_b=1000)

    copy_corrupt = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node.db, file=file_corrupt, has_file="X", wants_file="N"
    )
    copy_suspect = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node.db, file=file_suspect, has_file="M", wants_file="N"
    )
    copy_valid = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node.db, file=file_valid, has_file="Y", wants_file="N"
    )

    # Create UpdateableNode (already exists in mockgroupandnode)
    unode = UpdateableNode(queue, node.db)

    # Mock the I/O delete method
    with patch.object(unode.io, "delete") as mock_delete:
        unode.update_delete()

    # Collect all copy IDs passed to delete
    all_deleted_ids = set()
    for call_args in mock_delete.call_args_list:
        copies = call_args[0][0]  # first positional arg is the list of copies
        for c in copies:
            all_deleted_ids.add(c.id)

    assert copy_corrupt.id in all_deleted_ids, "Corrupt copy (X,N) was not deleted"
    assert copy_suspect.id in all_deleted_ids, "Suspect copy (M,N) was not deleted"
    assert copy_valid.id in all_deleted_ids, "Valid copy (Y,N) was not deleted"


def test_update_skips_check_for_bad_marked(xfs, mockgroupandnode, queue):
    """update should not check copies with has_file='M' and wants_file='N'."""
    mockio, group, node = mockgroupandnode

    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")
    file = ArchiveFile.create(name="file", acq=acq, size_b=1000)
    ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node.db, file=file, has_file="M", wants_file="N"
    )

    unode = UpdateableNode(queue, node.db)

    # Mock before_update to return True (allow update)
    with patch.object(unode.io, "before_update", return_value=True):
        with patch.object(unode.io, "check") as mock_check:
            unode.update()

    # check should not have been called because wants_file='N'
    mock_check.assert_not_called()


def test_update_checks_suspect_not_marked(xfs, mockgroupandnode, queue):
    """update should check copies with has_file='M' and wants_file='Y'."""
    mockio, group, node = mockgroupandnode

    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")
    file = ArchiveFile.create(name="file", acq=acq, size_b=1000)
    copy = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node.db, file=file, has_file="M", wants_file="Y"
    )

    unode = UpdateableNode(queue, node.db)

    with patch.object(unode.io, "before_update", return_value=True):
        with patch.object(unode.io, "check") as mock_check:
            unode.update()

    # check should have been called with this copy
    mock_check.assert_called_once_with(copy)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_clean_include_bad_flag_exists(clidb, cli):
    """The --include-bad flag should be accepted by node clean."""
    group = StorageGroup.create(name="Group")
    node = StorageNode.create(name="NODE", group=group, storage_type="F")
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")
    file = ArchiveFile.create(name="File", acq=acq, size_b=1000)
    ArchiveFileCopy.create(node=node, file=file, has_file="Y", wants_file="Y")

    # Just check that the option is accepted (no error)
    cli(0, ["node", "clean", "NODE", "--include-bad", "--force"])


def test_clean_include_bad_includes_corrupt(clidb, cli):
    """With --include-bad, corrupt files (has_file='X') should be included in cleaning."""
    group = StorageGroup.create(name="Group")
    node = StorageNode.create(name="NODE", group=group, storage_type="F")
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")

def test_clean_without_include_bad_skips_suspect(clidb, cli):

    copy = ArchiveFileCopy.get(node=node, file=file)
    assert copy.wants_file == "Y", f"Expected wants_file='Y', got '{copy.wants_file}'"

import pytest

from dishka import Provider, Scope, WithParents, provide_all, make_container


class TestProvideAllWithWithParents:
    """Tests for provide_all with WithParents."""

    def test_provide_all_with_withparents_no_type_error(self):
        """The original issue: provide_all(WithParents[MyImpl]) should not raise TypeError."""
        class A1:
            pass

        class A2(A1):
            pass

        class A3(A2):
            pass

        # This should not raise TypeError
        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            provides = provide_all(WithParents[A3])

        container = make_container(MyProvider())

        # All types should be retrievable
        a3 = container.get(A3)
        a2 = container.get(A2)
        a1 = container.get(A1)

        assert isinstance(a3, A3)
        assert isinstance(a2, A2)
        assert isinstance(a1, A1)

    def test_provide_all_with_withparents_mixed(self):
        """Mix of WithParents and regular types."""
        class A1:
            pass

        class A2(A1):
            pass

        class A3(A2):
            pass

        class RegularClass:
            pass

        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            provides = provide_all(WithParents[A3], RegularClass)

        container = make_container(MyProvider())

        a3 = container.get(A3)
        a2 = container.get(A2)
        a1 = container.get(A1)
        regular = container.get(RegularClass)

        assert isinstance(a3, A3)
        assert isinstance(a2, A2)
        assert isinstance(a1, A1)
        assert isinstance(regular, RegularClass)

    def test_provide_all_with_withparents_multiple_providers(self):
        """Multiple WithParents in one provide_all."""
        class A1:
            pass

        class A2(A1):
            pass

        class B1:
            pass

        class B2(B1):
            pass

        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            provides = provide_all(WithParents[A2], WithParents[B2])

        container = make_container(MyProvider())

        a2 = container.get(A2)
        a1 = container.get(A1)
        b2 = container.get(B2)
        b1 = container.get(B1)

        assert isinstance(a2, A2)
        assert isinstance(a1, A1)
        assert isinstance(b2, B2)
        assert isinstance(b1, B1)

    def test_provide_all_with_withparents_no_parents(self):
        """WithParents on a class with no parents (only object)."""
        class MyClass:
            pass

        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            provides = provide_all(WithParents[MyClass])

        container = make_container(MyProvider())

        obj = container.get(MyClass)
        assert isinstance(obj, MyClass)

        # object itself is not provided because WithParents excludes object
        with pytest.raises(Exception):
            container.get(object)

    def test_provide_all_with_withparents_request_scope(self):
        """WithParents works with REQUEST scope when properly opened."""
        class A1:
            pass

        class A2(A1):
            pass

        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.REQUEST
            provides = provide_all(WithParents[A2])

        container = make_container(MyProvider())

        # Open a request scope to get REQUEST-scoped dependencies
        with container() as request_container:
            a2 = request_container.get(A2)
            a1 = request_container.get(A1)

            assert isinstance(a2, A2)
            assert isinstance(a1, A1)

    def test_provide_all_with_withparents_separate_instances(self):
        """WithParents in provide_all creates separate instances for each type."""
        class A1:
            pass

        class A2(A1):
            pass

        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            provides = provide_all(WithParents[A2])

        container = make_container(MyProvider())

        a2 = container.get(A2)
        a1 = container.get(A1)

        # provide_all creates separate factories, so instances are different
        assert a2 is not a1

import io
import pytest

from csv2md.table import Table


def test_no_pipe_in_cell():
    """Cells without pipes should not be modified."""
    csv_data = '"a","b"\n"hello","world"'
    table = Table.parse_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))
    md = table.markdown()
    # The markdown should contain the original cell values unchanged
    assert "hello" in md
    assert "world" in md
    # No backslash should appear
    assert "\\" not in md


def test_single_pipe_in_cell():
    """A single pipe should be escaped with a backslash."""
    csv_data = '"a","b"\n"test|pipe","data"'
    table = Table.parse_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))
    md = table.markdown()
    # The cell should contain "test\|pipe"
    assert "test\\|pipe" in md


def test_multiple_pipes_in_cell():
    """Multiple pipes should all be escaped."""
    csv_data = '"a","b"\n"test|with|pipe|symbol","baz"'
    table = Table.parse_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))
    md = table.markdown()
    assert "test\\|with\\|pipe\\|symbol" in md


def test_already_escaped_pipes_not_double_escaped():
    """Cells that already contain backslash-escaped pipes should not get extra backslashes."""
    csv_data = '"a","b"\n"test\\|with\\|pipe\\|symbol","baz"'
    table = Table.parse_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))
    md = table.markdown()
    # The cell should remain "test\|with\|pipe\|symbol" (single backslash before each pipe)
    assert "test\\|with\\|pipe\\|symbol" in md
    # It should NOT contain double backslashes
    assert "test\\\\|with" not in md


def test_mixed_escaped_and_unescaped_pipes():
    """Mixed escaped and unescaped pipes: only unescaped pipes get backslashes."""
    csv_data = '"a","b"\n"pre\\|escaped|raw","val"'
    table = Table.parse_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))
    md = table.markdown()

"""
Tests for Store.list behavior regarding the delete parameter.

Issue: Store.list with delete=True should only list soft-deleted items,
and delete=False should only list non-deleted items.
Previously, delete=True listed both normal and soft-deleted items and
removed the .del suffix, making it impossible to distinguish.
"""

import pytest
from borgstore.store import Store, ItemInfo
from borgstore.constants import DEL_SUFFIX

LEVELS_CONFIG = {"zero/": [0], "one/": [1], "two/": [2]}


@pytest.fixture()
def store_created(tmp_path):
    url = f"file://{tmp_path}"
    store = Store(url=url, levels=LEVELS_CONFIG)
    store.create()
    try:
        yield store
    finally:
        store.destroy()


def test_list_deleted_false_only_non_deleted(store_created):
    """deleted=False must only yield items that are not soft-deleted."""
    ns = "zero"
    with store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/keep", b"data")
        store.store(f"{ns}/delete_me", b"data")
        store.move(f"{ns}/delete_me", delete=True)  # soft delete

        items = list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))
        names = [item.name for item in items]
        assert names == ["keep"]
        assert all(not name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX) for name in names)


def test_list_deleted_true_only_deleted(store_created):
    """deleted=True must only yield items that are soft-deleted."""
    ns = "zero"
    with store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/keep", b"data")
        store.store(f"{ns}/delete_me", b"data")
        store.move(f"{ns}/delete_me", delete=True)

        items = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))
        names = [item.name for item in items]
        assert names == ["delete_me" + DEL_SUFFIX]
        assert all(name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX) for name in names)


def test_list_deleted_disjoint_sets(store_created):
    """The sets returned by deleted=False and deleted=True must be disjoint."""
    ns = "zero"
    with store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/a", b"")
        store.store(f"{ns}/b", b"")
        store.store(f"{ns}/c", b"")
        store.move(f"{ns}/a", delete=True)
        store.move(f"{ns}/c", delete=True)

        normal = set(item.name for item in store.list(ns, deleted=False))
        deleted = set(item.name for item in store.list(ns, deleted=True))
        assert normal.isdisjoint(deleted)


def test_list_deleted_default_is_false(store_created):
    """Default value of deleted=False must behave like deleted=False."""
    ns = "zero"
    with store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/keep", b"")
        store.store(f"{ns}/del", b"")
        store.move(f"{ns}/del", delete=True)

        default = list(store.list(ns))
        explicit_false = list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))
        assert default == explicit_false


def test_list_empty_namespace(store_created):
    """Empty namespace must yield empty lists for both flags."""
    ns = "zero"
    with store_created as store:
        # Ensure the namespace directory exists by storing and deleting a dummy item
        store.store(f"{ns}/_dummy", b"")
        store.delete(f"{ns}/_dummy")
        assert list(store.list(ns, deleted=False)) == []
        assert list(store.list(ns, deleted=True)) == []


def test_list_all_deleted(store_created):
    """When all items are soft-deleted, deleted=False must be empty."""
    ns = "zero"
    with store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/x", b"")
        store.store(f"{ns}/y", b"")
        store.move(f"{ns}/x", delete=True)
        store.move(f"{ns}/y", delete=True)

        normal = list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))
        deleted = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))
        assert normal == []
        assert sorted(item.name for item in deleted) == ["x" + DEL_SUFFIX, "y" + DEL_SUFFIX]


def test_list_none_deleted(store_created):
    """When no items are soft-deleted, deleted=True must be empty."""
    ns = "zero"
    with store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/a", b"")
        store.store(f"{ns}/b", b"")

        normal = list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))
        deleted = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))
        assert sorted(item.name for item in normal) == ["a", "b"]
        assert deleted == []


def test_list_deleted_items_have_del_suffix(store_created):
    """Items yielded with deleted=True must have the .del suffix so caller can distinguish."""
    ns = "zero"
    with store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/item", b"")
        store.move(f"{ns}/item", delete=True)

        items = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))
        assert len(items) == 1
        assert items[0].name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX)
        # The original name without suffix should be recoverable
        original = items[0].name.removesuffix(DEL_SUFFIX)
        assert original == "item"


def test_list_non_deleted_items_no_del_suffix(store_created):
    """Items yielded with deleted=False must not have the .del suffix."""
    ns = "zero"
    with store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/item", b"")

        items = list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))
        assert len(items) == 1
        assert not items[0].name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX)


def test_list_mixed_namespace(store_created):
    """Mixed scenario: both deleted and non-deleted items present."""
    ns = "zero"
    with store_created as store:
        store.store(f"{ns}/a", b"")
        store.store(f"{ns}/b", b"")
        store.store(f"{ns}/c", b"")
        store.store(f"{ns}/d", b"")
        store.move(f"{ns}/a", delete=True)
        store.move(f"{ns}/c", delete=True)

        normal = set(item.name for item in store.list(ns, deleted=False))
        deleted = set(item.name for item in store.list(ns, deleted=True))
        assert normal == {"b", "d"}
        assert deleted == {"a" + DEL_SUFFIX, "c" + DEL_SUFFIX}
        # Union should cover all backend items (excluding directories)
        all_backend = set(info.name for info in store.backend.list(ns) if not info.directory)
        assert normal | deleted == all_backend

import pytest
from abc import abstractmethod
from typing import Protocol

from dishka import Provider, Scope, WithParents, make_container, provide_all


# --- Test helpers ---

class MyProtocol(Protocol):
    @abstractmethod
    def method(self) -> str: ...

class MyImpl(MyProtocol):
    def method(self) -> str:
        return "impl"

class Base:
    pass

class Derived(Base):
    pass

class InterfaceA(Protocol):
    def a(self) -> int: ...

class InterfaceB(Protocol):
    def b(self) -> str: ...

class MultiImpl(InterfaceA, InterfaceB):
    def a(self) -> int:
        return 1
    def b(self) -> str:
        return "b"


# --- Tests for provide_all with WithParents ---

class TestProvideAllWithParents:
    """Tests for the fix: provide_all(WithParents[...]) should work."""

    def test_provide_all_with_parents_creates_provider(self):
        """Reproduce the exact issue: no TypeError should be raised."""
        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            interactors = provide_all(WithParents[MyImpl])

        provider = MyProvider()
        # Should have at least one factory and possibly aliases
        assert len(provider.factories) > 0

    def test_provide_all_with_parents_container_get_concrete(self):
        """Container should be able to get the concrete class."""
        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            interactors = provide_all(WithParents[MyImpl])

        container = make_container(MyProvider())
        impl = container.get(MyImpl)
        assert isinstance(impl, MyImpl)
        assert impl.method() == "impl"

    def test_provide_all_with_parents_container_get_protocol(self):
        """Container should be able to get the protocol (parent)."""
        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            interactors = provide_all(WithParents[MyImpl])

        container = make_container(MyProvider())
        proto = container.get(MyProtocol)
        assert isinstance(proto, MyImpl)
        assert proto.method() == "impl"

    def test_provide_all_with_parents_same_instance(self):
        """Concrete class and protocol should be the same instance."""
        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            interactors = provide_all(WithParents[MyImpl])

        container = make_container(MyProvider())
        impl = container.get(MyImpl)
        proto = container.get(MyProtocol)
        assert impl is proto

    def test_provide_all_with_parents_simple_inheritance(self):
        """Test with a simple base class (not protocol)."""
        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            interactors = provide_all(WithParents[Derived])

        container = make_container(MyProvider())
        derived = container.get(Derived)
        base = container.get(Base)
        assert isinstance(derived, Derived)
        assert isinstance(base, Base)
        assert derived is base

    def test_provide_all_with_parents_multiple_inheritance(self):
        """Test with a class implementing multiple protocols."""
        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            interactors = provide_all(WithParents[MultiImpl])

        container = make_container(MyProvider())
        impl = container.get(MultiImpl)
        iface_a = container.get(InterfaceA)
        iface_b = container.get(InterfaceB)
        assert impl is iface_a is iface_b
        assert iface_a.a() == 1
        assert iface_b.b() == "b"

    def test_provide_all_with_parents_multiple_types(self):
        """Test provide_all with multiple WithParents arguments."""
        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            interactors = provide_all(
                WithParents[MyImpl],
                WithParents[Derived],
            )

        container = make_container(MyProvider())
        impl = container.get(MyImpl)
        derived = container.get(Derived)
        assert isinstance(impl, MyImpl)
        assert isinstance(derived, Derived)

    def test_provide_all_mixed_with_parents_and_regular(self):
        """Test mixing WithParents with a regular type in provide_all."""
        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            interactors = provide_all(
                WithParents[MyImpl],
                Derived,  # regular class without WithParents
            )

        container = make_container(MyProvider())
        impl = container.get(MyImpl)
        derived = container.get(Derived)
        assert isinstance(impl, MyImpl)
        assert isinstance(derived, Derived)

    def test_provide_all_with_parents_no_parents(self):
        """Test WithParents on a class with no extra parents (only object)."""
        class Standalone:
            pass

        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            interactors = provide_all(WithParents[Standalone])

        container = make_container(MyProvider())
        obj = container.get(Standalone)
        assert isinstance(obj, Standalone)

    def test_provide_all_with_parents_scope_request(self):
        """Test with REQUEST scope (requires context manager)."""
        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.REQUEST
            interactors = provide_all(WithParents[MyImpl])

        container = make_container(MyProvider())
        with container() as c:
            impl = c.get(MyImpl)
            proto = c.get(MyProtocol)
            assert impl is proto
            assert impl.method() == "impl"


# --- Tests that existing provide_all behavior is unchanged ---

class TestProvideAllRegular:
    """Ensure provide_all without WithParents still works."""

    def test_provide_all_regular_class(self):
        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            items = provide_all(MyImpl, Derived)

        container = make_container(MyProvider())
        impl = container.get(MyImpl)
        derived = container.get(Derived)
        assert isinstance(impl, MyImpl)
        assert isinstance(derived, Derived)

    def test_provide_all_regular_class_with_protocol(self):
        """Without WithParents, protocol is not automatically provided."""
        class MyProvider(Provider):
            scope = Scope.APP
            items = provide_all(MyImpl)

        container = make_container(MyProvider())
        impl = container.get(MyImpl)
        assert isinstance(impl, MyImpl)
        # MyProtocol should not be provided automatically
        with pytest.raises(Exception):
            container.get(MyProtocol)

"""
Tests for Store.list with delete parameter.

Issue: Store.list with delete=True vs. =False
- False will only list not-deleted objects
- True will only list soft-deleted objects
"""

import pytest
from borgstore.store import Store, ItemInfo
from borgstore.constants import DEL_SUFFIX
from . import key, list_store_names, list_store_names_sorted
from .test_backends import get_posixfs_test_backend

LEVELS_CONFIG = {"zero/": [0], "one/": [1], "two/": [2]}


@pytest.fixture()
def posixfs_store_created(tmp_path):
    store = Store(backend=get_posixfs_test_backend(tmp_path), levels=LEVELS_CONFIG)
    store.create()
    try:
        yield store
    finally:
        store.destroy()


class TestListDeleted:
    """Test Store.list with delete parameter."""

    def test_list_deleted_false_only_non_deleted(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """deleted=False should only list items that are not soft-deleted."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/item1", b"data1")
            store.store(f"{ns}/item2", b"data2")
            store.store(f"{ns}/item3", b"data3")

            # Soft delete item1
            store.move(f"{ns}/item1", delete=True)

            normal = list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))
            normal_names = [item.name for item in normal]

            assert "item1" not in normal_names, "deleted item should not appear in deleted=False"
            assert "item2" in normal_names
            assert "item3" in normal_names
            assert len(normal_names) == 2

    def test_list_deleted_true_only_deleted(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """deleted=True should only list soft-deleted items (with .del suffix)."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/item1", b"data1")
            store.store(f"{ns}/item2", b"data2")
            store.store(f"{ns}/item3", b"data3")

            # Soft delete item1 and item3
            store.move(f"{ns}/item1", delete=True)
            store.move(f"{ns}/item3", delete=True)

            deleted = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))
            deleted_names = [item.name for item in deleted]

            # Should only contain deleted items with .del suffix
            assert "item1.del" in deleted_names
            assert "item3.del" in deleted_names
            assert "item2" not in deleted_names
            assert len(deleted_names) == 2

    def test_list_deleted_true_preserves_del_suffix(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """The .del suffix must be preserved so caller can distinguish deleted items."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/item1", b"data1")
            store.move(f"{ns}/item1", delete=True)

            deleted = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))
            assert len(deleted) == 1
            item = deleted[0]
            assert item.name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX), f"Deleted item name should end with {DEL_SUFFIX!r}"
            assert item.name == "item1.del"

    def test_list_no_overlap(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """Results from deleted=False and deleted=True should have no overlap."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/a", b"1")
            store.store(f"{ns}/b", b"2")
            store.move(f"{ns}/a", delete=True)

            normal = set(item.name for item in store.list(ns, deleted=False))
            deleted = set(item.name for item in store.list(ns, deleted=True))

            assert normal.isdisjoint(deleted), "Normal and deleted sets should be disjoint"

    def test_list_empty_store(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """Empty store should return empty lists for both modes."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            # First ensure the namespace exists by storing and deleting an item
            store.store(f"{ns}/dummy", b"x")
            store.delete(f"{ns}/dummy")
            # Now the namespace exists but has no items
            normal = list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))
            deleted = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))
            assert normal == []
            assert deleted == []

    def test_list_all_deleted(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """When all items are soft-deleted, deleted=False returns empty, deleted=True returns all."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/x", b"1")
            store.store(f"{ns}/y", b"2")
            store.move(f"{ns}/x", delete=True)
            store.move(f"{ns}/y", delete=True)

            normal = list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))
            deleted = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))

            assert normal == []
            assert sorted([item.name for item in deleted]) == ["x.del", "y.del"]

    def test_list_none_deleted(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """When no items are soft-deleted, deleted=True returns empty, deleted=False returns all."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/a", b"1")
            store.store(f"{ns}/b", b"2")

            normal = list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))
            deleted = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))

            assert sorted([item.name for item in normal]) == ["a", "b"]
            assert deleted == []

    def test_list_after_undelete(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """After undeleting, the item should move from deleted=True to deleted=False."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/item", b"data")
            store.move(f"{ns}/item", delete=True)

            # Before undelete
            assert len(list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))) == 1
            assert len(list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))) == 0

            # Undelete
            store.move(f"{ns}/item", undelete=True)

            # After undelete
            assert len(list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))) == 0
            assert len(list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))) == 1

    def test_list_with_nesting(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """Test with nested namespace (level 1)."""
        ns = "one"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/00000000", b"data")
            store.store(f"{ns}/00000001", b"data")
            store.move(f"{ns}/00000000", delete=True)

            normal = list(store.list(ns, deleted=False))
            deleted = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))

            assert [item.name for item in normal] == ["00000001"]
            assert [item.name for item in deleted] == ["00000000.del"]

    def test_list_default_deleted_false(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """Default value of deleted should be False (backward compatibility)."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/keep", b"1")
            store.store(f"{ns}/remove", b"2")
            store.move(f"{ns}/remove", delete=True)

            # Calling list without deleted argument should default to False
            result = list(store.list(ns))
            names = [item.name for item in result]
            assert "keep" in names
            assert "remove" not in names
            assert len(names) == 1

    def test_list_item_info_correct(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """ItemInfo returned should have correct attributes."""
        ns = "zero"
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store(f"{ns}/item", b"hello")
            store.move(f"{ns}/item", delete=True)

            deleted_items = list(store.list(ns, deleted=True))
            assert len(deleted_items) == 1
            info = deleted_items[0]
            assert info.name == "item.del"
            assert info.exists is True
            assert info.directory is False
            assert info.size == 5  # length of b"hello"

    def test_list_multiple_namespaces(self, posixfs_store_created):
        """Different namespaces should be independent."""
        with posixfs_store_created as store:
            store.store("zero/a", b"1")
            store.store("one/b", b"2")
            store.move("zero/a", delete=True)

            one_normal = list(store.list("one", deleted=False))

            assert zero_normal == []
            assert [item.name for item in one_normal] == ["b"]

import pytest
from typing import Protocol
from abc import abstractmethod

from dishka import Provider, Scope, WithParents, provide_all, make_container
from dishka.entities.provides_marker import ProvideMultiple
from dishka.dependency_source.make_factory import _provide_all


# --- Test classes ---
class BaseClass:
    pass

class DerivedClass(BaseClass):
    pass

class MyProtocol(Protocol):
    @abstractmethod
    def method(self) -> str: ...

class MyImpl(MyProtocol):
    def method(self) -> str:
        return "impl"

class InterfaceA(Protocol):
    def method_a(self) -> str: ...

class InterfaceB(Protocol):
    def method_b(self) -> int: ...

class MultiImpl(InterfaceA, InterfaceB):
    def method_a(self) -> str:
        return "A"
    def method_b(self) -> int:
        return 42


# --- Tests ---

def test_provide_all_withparents_creates_factories():
    """provide_all(WithParents[MyImpl]) should not raise and create factories."""
    class MyProvider(Provider):
        scope = Scope.APP
        impl = provide_all(WithParents[MyImpl])

    provider = MyProvider()
    # Should have at least one factory (for MyImpl) and aliases for parents
    assert len(provider.factories) >= 1
    # Check that the factory provides the ProvideMultiple (WithParents)
    factory = provider.factories[0]
    assert factory.provides.type_hint is not None
    # The source should be MyImpl (the concrete class)
    assert factory.source is MyImpl


def test_provide_all_withparents_resolves_class():
    """Container should be able to get MyImpl and its parent protocol."""
    class MyProvider(Provider):
        scope = Scope.APP
        impl = provide_all(WithParents[MyImpl])

    provider = MyProvider()
    container = make_container(provider)
    impl = container.get(MyImpl)
    assert isinstance(impl, MyImpl)
    proto = container.get(MyProtocol)
    assert isinstance(proto, MyImpl)
    assert impl is proto  # same instance


def test_provide_all_withparents_simple_inheritance():
    """WithParents on a simple class should also provide base class."""
    class MyProvider(Provider):
        scope = Scope.APP
        derived = provide_all(WithParents[DerivedClass])

    provider = MyProvider()
    container = make_container(provider)
    derived = container.get(DerivedClass)
    base = container.get(BaseClass)
    assert isinstance(derived, DerivedClass)
    assert isinstance(base, DerivedClass)
    assert derived is base


def test_provide_all_withparents_multiple_inheritance():
    """WithParents on a class with multiple protocol parents."""
    class MyProvider(Provider):
        scope = Scope.APP
        multi = provide_all(WithParents[MultiImpl])

    provider = MyProvider()
    container = make_container(provider)
    multi = container.get(MultiImpl)
    a = container.get(InterfaceA)
    b = container.get(InterfaceB)
    assert isinstance(multi, MultiImpl)
    assert isinstance(a, MultiImpl)
    assert isinstance(b, MultiImpl)
    assert multi is a is b

"""Tests for cross_validate with multiple scoring metrics (issue #TTG)."""

import numpy as np
import pytest
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingRegressor
from sklearn.linear_model import Lasso
from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix

from skore import cross_validate
from skore.item.cross_validation_aggregation_item import CrossValidationAggregationItem
from skore.item.cross_validation_item import CrossValidationItem


class TestCrossValidateMultipleScoring:
    """Verify that cross_validate works with various scoring inputs,
    especially lists and tuples, and that aggregation does not raise
    ``ValueError: cannot reindex on an axis with duplicate labels``."""

    @pytest.fixture
    def small_regression_data(self):
        """Return a small regression dataset (20 samples)."""
        rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
        X = rng.rand(20, 3)
        y = rng.rand(20)
        return X, y

    @pytest.fixture
    def tiny_regression_data(self):
        """Return a tiny dataset (5 samples) as in the issue."""
        X = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]).reshape(-1, 1)
        y = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
        return X, y

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def _run_and_aggregate(project, estimator, X, y, *, scoring, cv=3):
        """Run cross_validate twice with the same key to trigger aggregation."""
        for _ in range(2):
            cross_validate(estimator, X, y, cv=cv, scoring=scoring, project=project)
        # Force aggregation by retrieving the item versions
        items = project.get_item_versions("cross_validation")
        CrossValidationAggregationItem.factory(items)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tests – list / tuple scoring (the core of the issue)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_list_of_strings(self, in_memory_project, small_regression_data):
        """List of metric strings should not raise."""
        X, y = small_regression_data
        self._run_and_aggregate(
            in_memory_project,
            HistGradientBoostingRegressor(),
            X,
            y,
            scoring=["neg_mean_absolute_error", "r2", "explained_variance"],
        )

    def test_tuple_of_strings(self, in_memory_project, small_regression_data):
        """Tuple of metric strings should not raise."""
        X, y = small_regression_data
        self._run_and_aggregate(
            in_memory_project,
            HistGradientBoostingRegressor(),
            X,
            y,
            scoring=("r2", "neg_mean_absolute_error"),
        )

    def test_single_element_tuple(self, in_memory_project, small_regression_data):
        """Single-element tuple (e.g. ``("r2",)``) should not raise."""
        X, y = small_regression_data
        self._run_and_aggregate(
            in_memory_project,
            HistGradientBoostingRegressor(),
            X,
            y,
            scoring=("r2",),
        )

    def test_single_string(self, in_memory_project, small_regression_data):
        """Single string scoring should still work."""
        X, y = small_regression_data
        self._run_and_aggregate(
            in_memory_project,
            HistGradientBoostingRegressor(),
            X,
            y,
            scoring="r2",
        )

    def test_none_scoring(self, in_memory_project, small_regression_data):
        """``scoring=None`` should not raise."""
        X, y = small_regression_data
        self._run_and_aggregate(
            in_memory_project,
            HistGradientBoostingRegressor(),
            X,
            y,
            scoring=None,
        )

    def test_dict_scoring(self, in_memory_project, small_regression_data):
        """Dictionary of metric name -> callable/string should not raise."""
        X, y = small_regression_data
        self._run_and_aggregate(
            in_memory_project,
            HistGradientBoostingRegressor(),
            X,
            y,
            scoring={"mae": "neg_mean_absolute_error", "r2": "r2"},
        )

    def test_callable_returning_float(self, in_memory_project, small_regression_data):
        """Callable returning a single float should not raise."""
        X, y = small_regression_data

        def my_scorer(estimator, X, y_true):
            y_pred = estimator.predict(X)
            return float(np.mean(np.abs(y_true - y_pred)))

        self._run_and_aggregate(
            in_memory_project,
            HistGradientBoostingRegressor(),
            X,
            y,
            scoring=my_scorer,
        )

    def test_callable_returning_dict(self, in_memory_project, small_regression_data):
        """Callable returning a dict should not raise."""
        X, y = small_regression_data

        def my_dict_scorer(estimator, X, y_true):
            y_pred = estimator.predict(X)
            mae = float(np.mean(np.abs(y_true - y_pred)))
            mse = float(np.mean((y_true - y_pred) ** 2))
            return {"mae": mae, "mse": mse}

        self._run_and_aggregate(
            in_memory_project,
            HistGradientBoostingRegressor(),
            X,
            y,
            scoring=my_dict_scorer,
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Edge cases from the issue
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_tiny_dataset_with_cv5(self, in_memory_project, tiny_regression_data):
        """Reproduce the exact scenario from the issue: 5 samples, cv=5,
        multiple metrics.  Should not raise (warnings about R² are fine)."""
        X, y = tiny_regression_data
        # Use a fast linear model to avoid long runtime
        self._run_and_aggregate(
            in_memory_project,
            Lasso(),
            X,
            y,
            cv=5,
            scoring=["neg_mean_absolute_error", "r2", "explained_variance"],
        )

    def test_tiny_dataset_tuple_scoring(self, in_memory_project, tiny_regression_data):
        """Reproduce the tuple case from the issue: 5 samples, cv=3,
        ``scoring=("r2",)``."""
        X, y = tiny_regression_data
        self._run_and_aggregate(
            in_memory_project,
            Lasso(),
            X,
            y,
            cv=3,
            scoring=("r2",),
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Additional robustness checks
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_different_estimators(self, in_memory_project, small_regression_data):
        """Works with different estimator types (regression)."""
        X, y = small_regression_data
        self._run_and_aggregate(
            in_memory_project,
            Lasso(),
            X,
            y,
            scoring=["r2", "neg_mean_absolute_error"],
        )

    def test_aggregation_with_single_item(self, in_memory_project, small_regression_data):
        """Aggregation with only one version should also work."""
        X, y = small_regression_data
        reporter = cross_validate(
            HistGradientBoostingRegressor(),
            X,
            y,
            cv=3,
            scoring=["r2", "neg_mean_absolute_error"],
            project=in_memory_project,
        )
        items = in_memory_project.get_item_versions("cross_validation")
        CrossValidationAggregationItem.factory(items)

    def test_no_project_usage(self, small_regression_data):
        """Calling cross_validate without a project should not raise."""
        X, y = small_regression_data
        cross_validate(
            HistGradientBoostingRegressor(),
            X,
            y,
            cv=3,
            scoring=["neg_mean_absolute_error", "r2"],
        )

    def test_return_estimator_and_indices(self, in_memory_project, small_regression_data):
        """Using return_estimator=True and return_indices=True should not break."""
        X, y = small_regression_data
        self._run_and_aggregate(
            in_memory_project,
            HistGradientBoostingRegressor(),
            X,
            y,
            cv=3,
            scoring=["r2"],
        )
        # Note: cross_validate does not expose return_estimator/return_indices
        # directly; they are passed through to sklearn.  We test that the
        # reporter handles them correctly.
        from skore import CrossValidationReporter
        reporter = CrossValidationReporter(
            HistGradientBoostingRegressor(),
            X,
            y,
            cv=3,
            scoring=["r2"],
            return_estimator=True,
            return_indices=True,
        )
        in_memory_project.put("cv2", reporter)
        in_memory_project.put("cv2", reporter)
        items = in_memory_project.get_item_versions("cv2")
        CrossValidationAggregationItem.factory(items)
