import os
import tempfile
import pytest
from checkov.cloudformation.runner import Runner
from checkov.runner_filter import RunnerFilter

# CKV_AWS_24 is a built-in check that flags security groups with SSH port open to 0.0.0.0/0
# We'll use it to test suppression.

YAML_TEMPLATE_WITH_SUPPRESSION = """\
Description: Test suppression
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:{comment}
  TestSG:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Test SG
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""

YAML_TEMPLATE_NO_SUPPRESSION = """\
Description: Test no suppression
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  TestSG:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Test SG
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""

YAML_TEMPLATE_MULTIPLE = """\
Description: Test multiple resources
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:Suppressed SG
  SuppressedSG:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Suppressed SG
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
  NotSuppressedSG:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Not suppressed SG
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""


def _run_checkov(template_content, suffix=".yaml", check_id="CKV_AWS_24"):
    """Helper to run checkov on a temporary file and return the report."""
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", suffix=suffix, delete=False) as f:
        f.write(template_content)
        tmp_path = f.name
    try:
        runner = Runner()
        report = runner.run(
            root_folder=None,
            files=[tmp_path],
            runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=[check_id])
        )
        return report
    finally:
        os.unlink(tmp_path)


class TestCloudFormationSuppression:
    """Tests for CloudFormation suppression (skip comments)."""

    def test_suppression_basic(self):
        """A resource with a skip comment should be skipped."""
        report = _run_checkov(
            YAML_TEMPLATE_WITH_SUPPRESSION.format(comment="test comment")
        )
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 0
        skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
        assert skipped.check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
        assert "test comment" in skipped.check_result.get("suppress_comment", "")

    def test_no_suppression(self):
        """A resource without a skip comment should fail."""
        report = _run_checkov(YAML_TEMPLATE_NO_SUPPRESSION)
        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 0
        assert report.failed_checks[0].check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"

    def test_suppression_multiple_resources(self):
        """Only the resource with a skip comment should be skipped; the other should fail."""
        report = _run_checkov(YAML_TEMPLATE_MULTIPLE)
        # One suppressed, one failed
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1
        skipped_resource = report.skipped_checks[0].resource
        failed_resource = report.failed_checks[0].resource
        assert "SuppressedSG" in skipped_resource
        assert "NotSuppressedSG" in failed_resource

    def test_suppression_comment_formats(self):
        """Test various comment formats: no space after #, space after #, no comment text."""
        # Format: #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: (no comment)
        report = _run_checkov(
            YAML_TEMPLATE_WITH_SUPPRESSION.format(comment="")
        )
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
        skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
        assert skipped.check_result.get("suppress_comment") == "No comment provided"

        # Format: # checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: comment with space after #
        template_with_space = YAML_TEMPLATE_WITH_SUPPRESSION.replace(
            "#checkov:skip=", "# checkov:skip="
        ).format(comment="space after hash")
        report = _run_checkov(template_with_space)
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
        skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
        assert "space after hash" in skipped.check_result.get("suppress_comment", "")

        # Format: #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:Comment without space after colon
        template_no_space_colon = YAML_TEMPLATE_WITH_SUPPRESSION.format(
            comment="NoSpaceAfterColon"
        )
        report = _run_checkov(template_no_space_colon)
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
        skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
        assert "NoSpaceAfterColon" in skipped.check_result.get("suppress_comment", "")

    def test_suppression_comment_not_applied_to_wrong_resource(self):
        """A skip comment should only apply to the immediately following resource."""
        template = """\
Description: Test comment proximity
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:This comment is for SG1
  SG1:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: SG1
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
  SG2:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: SG2
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""
        report = _run_checkov(template)
        # SG1 should be skipped, SG2 should fail
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1
        assert "SG1" in report.skipped_checks[0].resource
        assert "SG2" in report.failed_checks[0].resource

    def test_suppression_with_multiple_checks(self):
        """If multiple skip comments are present, only the closest one is used."""
        template = """\
Description: Test multiple skip comments
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:First comment
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:Second comment (closest)
  SG:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: SG
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""
        report = _run_checkov(template)
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
        skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
        # The closest comment (second) should be used
        assert "Second comment" in skipped.check_result.get("suppress_comment", "")

"""Tests for the publish-lib command exit code fix."""

import argparse
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

import pytest
from craft_application import AppMetadata

from charmcraft.application.commands.store import PublishLibCommand


@pytest.fixture
def mock_services():
    """Create a mock services object with a store."""
    services = MagicMock()
    services.store = MagicMock()
    return services


@pytest.fixture
def publish_lib_command(mock_services):
    """Create a PublishLibCommand instance with mocked services and app."""
    app = MagicMock(spec=AppMetadata)
    config = {
        "app": app,
        "services": mock_services,
    }
    cmd = PublishLibCommand(config)
    return cmd


def _make_lib_data(name="test_lib", api=0, patch=1, content_hash="abc"):
    """Create a minimal lib_data dict as expected by the command."""
    return {
        "charm_name": "test-charm",
        "lib_name": name,
        "api": api,
        "patch": patch,
        "content_hash": content_hash,
        "lib_path": "/fake/path.py",
        "lib_id": "test-id",
    }


def test_publish_lib_success(publish_lib_command, mock_services, emitter):
    """Test that publish-lib returns 0 when all libraries publish successfully."""
    lib_data = _make_lib_data()
    analysis = [(lib_data, None)]  # no error

    with patch.object(
        publish_lib_command, "_get_libs_data", return_value=analysis
    ):
        parsed_args = argparse.Namespace(
            libraries=["test-charm/test_lib"],
            format=None,
        )
        result = publish_lib_command.run(parsed_args)

    assert result == 0, "Expected exit code 0 on success"
    mock_services.store.create_library_revision.assert_called_once_with(
        lib_data["charm_name"],
        lib_data["lib_id"],
        lib_data["api"],
        lib_data["patch"],
        lib_data["content_hash"],
        lib_data["lib_path"],
    )
    emitter.assert_message("Library test_lib v0.1 pushed")


def test_publish_lib_failure(publish_lib_command, mock_services, emitter):
    """Test that publish-lib returns 1 when a library fails to publish."""
    lib_data = _make_lib_data()
    error_msg = "LIBPATCH is not bumped"
    analysis = [(lib_data, error_msg)]

    with patch.object(
        publish_lib_command, "_get_libs_data", return_value=analysis
    ):
        parsed_args = argparse.Namespace(
            libraries=["test-charm/test_lib"],
            format=None,
        )
        result = publish_lib_command.run(parsed_args)

    assert result == 1, "Expected exit code 1 on failure"
    mock_services.store.create_library_revision.assert_not_called()
    emitter.assert_message(error_msg)


def test_publish_lib_mixed(publish_lib_command, mock_services, emitter):
    """Test that publish-lib returns 1 when some libraries fail and some succeed."""
    lib_data_ok = _make_lib_data(name="lib_ok")
    lib_data_fail = _make_lib_data(name="lib_fail")
    error_msg = "LIBPATCH going back"
    analysis = [
        (lib_data_ok, None),
        (lib_data_fail, error_msg),
    ]

    with patch.object(
        publish_lib_command, "_get_libs_data", return_value=analysis
    ):
        parsed_args = argparse.Namespace(
            libraries=["test-charm/lib_ok", "test-charm/lib_fail"],
            format=None,
        )
        result = publish_lib_command.run(parsed_args)

    assert result == 1, "Expected exit code 1 when any library fails"
    # Only the successful library should be published
    mock_services.store.create_library_revision.assert_called_once_with(
        lib_data_ok["charm_name"],
        lib_data_ok["lib_id"],
        lib_data_ok["api"],
        lib_data_ok["patch"],
        lib_data_ok["content_hash"],
        lib_data_ok["lib_path"],
    )
    emitter.assert_message("Library lib_ok v0.1 pushed")
    emitter.assert_message(error_msg)


def test_publish_lib_multiple_failures(publish_lib_command, mock_services, emitter):
    """Test that publish-lib returns 1 when multiple libraries fail."""
    lib_data_1 = _make_lib_data(name="lib1")
    lib_data_2 = _make_lib_data(name="lib2")
    error_msg_1 = "LIBPATCH is not bumped"
    error_msg_2 = "Library not found"
    analysis = [
        (lib_data_1, error_msg_1),
        (lib_data_2, error_msg_2),
    ]

    with patch.object(
        publish_lib_command, "_get_libs_data", return_value=analysis
    ):
        parsed_args = argparse.Namespace(
            libraries=["test-charm/lib1", "test-charm/lib2"],
            format=None,
        )
        result = publish_lib_command.run(parsed_args)

    assert result == 1, "Expected exit code 1 when all libraries fail"
    mock_services.store.create_library_revision.assert_not_called()
    emitter.assert_message(error_msg_1)
    emitter.assert_message(error_msg_2)


def test_publish_lib_no_libraries(publish_lib_command, mock_services, emitter):
    """Test that publish-lib returns 0 when there are no libraries to publish."""
    analysis = []

    with patch.object(
        publish_lib_command, "_get_libs_data", return_value=analysis
    ):
        parsed_args = argparse.Namespace(
            libraries=[],
            format=None,
        )
        result = publish_lib_command.run(parsed_args)

    assert result == 0, "Expected exit code 0 when no libraries"
    mock_services.store.create_library_revision.assert_not_called()

        data = [{"range": "A1:B2", "values": [["a", "b"]]}]
        result = ws.batch_update(
            data,
            raw=False,
            value_input_option=ValueInputOption.user_entered,
            include_values_in_response=True,
            response_value_render_option=ValueRenderOption.formatted,
            response_date_time_render_option=DateTimeOption.serial_number,
        )
        expected_body = {
            "valueInputOption": ValueInputOption.user_entered,
            "includeValuesInResponse": True,
            "responseValueRenderOption": ValueRenderOption.formatted,
            "responseDateTimeRenderOption": DateTimeOption.serial_number,
            "data": [{"range": "'Sheet1'!A1:B2", "values": [["a", "b"]]}],
        }
        client.values_batch_update.assert_called_once_with(
            "fake_spreadsheet", body=expected_body
        )

import numpy as np
import pytest
from supervision.detection.utils import move_masks


def test_move_masks_positive_offset():
    """
    Test that a mask is correctly shifted by a positive offset.
    """
    # Create a 1x4x4 mask with a 2x2 block of True at top-left corner
    masks = np.zeros((1, 4, 4), dtype=bool)
    masks[0, 0:2, 0:2] = True

    offset = np.array([2, 1])  # dx=2, dy=1
    resolution_wh = (6, 5)     # width=6, height=5

    result = move_masks(masks, offset, resolution_wh)

    # Expected: the 2x2 block should appear at (dx, dy) = (2, 1)
    expected = np.zeros((1, 5, 6), dtype=bool)
    expected[0, 1:3, 2:4] = True

    assert result.shape == (1, 5, 6)
    assert np.array_equal(result, expected), f"Positive offset failed.\nResult:\n{result[0]}\nExpected:\n{expected[0]}"


def test_move_masks_negative_offset():
    """
    Test that a mask is correctly shifted by a negative offset (moving up/left).
    """
    # Create a 1x5x5 mask with a 2x2 block at (2,2) (row=2, col=2)
    masks = np.zeros((1, 5, 5), dtype=bool)
    masks[0, 2:4, 2:4] = True

    offset = np.array([-1, -2])  # dx=-1, dy=-2
    resolution_wh = (5, 5)

    result = move_masks(masks, offset, resolution_wh)

    # The block should move to (2-1, 2-2) = (1, 0) -> rows 0..2, cols 1..3
    expected = np.zeros((1, 5, 5), dtype=bool)
    expected[0, 0:2, 1:3] = True

    assert result.shape == (1, 5, 5)
    assert np.array_equal(result, expected), f"Negative offset failed.\nResult:\n{result[0]}\nExpected:\n{expected[0]}"


def test_move_masks_mixed_offset():
    """
    Test with mixed signs: positive dx, negative dy.
    """
    masks = np.zeros((1, 4, 4), dtype=bool)
    masks[0, 1:3, 1:3] = True  # 2x2 block at (1,1)

    offset = np.array([3, -1])  # dx=3, dy=-1
    resolution_wh = (8, 6)

    result = move_masks(masks, offset, resolution_wh)

    # Block moves to (1+3, 1-1) = (4, 0) -> rows 0..2, cols 4..6
    expected = np.zeros((1, 6, 8), dtype=bool)
    expected[0, 0:2, 4:6] = True

    assert result.shape == (1, 6, 8)
    assert np.array_equal(result, expected), f"Mixed offset failed.\nResult:\n{result[0]}\nExpected:\n{expected[0]}"


def test_move_masks_zero_offset():
    """
    Zero offset should leave the mask unchanged (but placed in a possibly larger canvas).
    """
    masks = np.zeros((1, 3, 3), dtype=bool)
    masks[0, 0, 0] = True
    masks[0, 2, 2] = True

    offset = np.array([0, 0])
    resolution_wh = (3, 3)

    result = move_masks(masks, offset, resolution_wh)

    assert result.shape == (1, 3, 3)
    assert np.array_equal(result, masks), f"Zero offset should preserve mask."


def test_move_masks_large_positive_offset_out_of_bounds():
    """
    When the offset moves the mask completely out of the resolution,
    the result should be all False.
    """
    masks = np.ones((1, 2, 2), dtype=bool)  # full 2x2 True
    offset = np.array([10, 10])
    resolution_wh = (5, 5)

    result = move_masks(masks, offset, resolution_wh)

    assert result.shape == (1, 5, 5)
    assert not np.any(result), "Mask should be completely out of bounds."


def test_move_masks_large_negative_offset_out_of_bounds():
    """
    Negative offset that moves the mask completely out of bounds.
    """
    masks = np.ones((1, 2, 2), dtype=bool)
    offset = np.array([-10, -10])
    resolution_wh = (5, 5)

    result = move_masks(masks, offset, resolution_wh)

    assert result.shape == (1, 5, 5)
    assert not np.any(result), "Mask should be completely out of bounds."


def test_move_masks_partial_crop_positive():
    """
    Positive offset that causes part of the mask to be cropped on the right/bottom.
    """
    masks = np.zeros((1, 4, 4), dtype=bool)
    masks[0, 0:4, 0:4] = True  # full 4x4

    offset = np.array([2, 2])
    resolution_wh = (5, 5)  # only 5x5 canvas

    result = move_masks(masks, offset, resolution_wh)

    # Only the top-left 3x3 of the original mask fits (since offset 2,2 -> rows 2..4, cols 2..4)
    expected = np.zeros((1, 5, 5), dtype=bool)
    expected[0, 2:5, 2:5] = True  # rows 2..4 (3 rows), cols 2..4 (3 cols)

    assert result.shape == (1, 5, 5)
    assert np.array_equal(result, expected), f"Partial crop positive failed.\nResult:\n{result[0]}\nExpected:\n{expected[0]}"


def test_move_masks_partial_crop_negative():
    """
    Negative offset that causes part of the mask to be cropped on the left/top.
    """
    masks = np.zeros((1, 4, 4), dtype=bool)
    masks[0, 0:4, 0:4] = True  # full 4x4

    offset = np.array([-1, -2])
    resolution_wh = (5, 5)

    result = move_masks(masks, offset, resolution_wh)

    # Original mask moves left by 1 and up by 2.
    # Only the bottom-right 3x2 of the original mask remains (rows 2..4, cols 1..4)
    expected = np.zeros((1, 5, 5), dtype=bool)
    expected[0, 0:2, 0:3] = True  # rows 0..1 (2 rows), cols 0..2 (3 cols)

    assert result.shape == (1, 5, 5)
    assert np.array_equal(result, expected), f"Partial crop negative failed.\nResult:\n{result[0]}\nExpected:\n{expected[0]}"


def test_move_masks_multiple_masks():
    """
    Test that multiple masks are all moved independently.
    """
    masks = np.zeros((2, 5, 5), dtype=bool)
    masks[0, 0:2, 0:2] = True  # first mask: top-left 2x2
    masks[1, 3:5, 3:5] = True  # second mask: bottom-right 2x2

    offset = np.array([1, 1])
    resolution_wh = (6, 6)

    result = move_masks(masks, offset, resolution_wh)

    expected = np.zeros((2, 6, 6), dtype=bool)
    expected[0, 1:3, 1:3] = True
    expected[1, 4:6, 4:6] = True

    assert result.shape == (2, 6, 6)
    assert np.array_equal(result, expected), f"Multiple masks failed."


def test_move_masks_empty_masks():
    """
    Edge case: empty mask array (N=0) should return an empty array of the given resolution.
    """
    masks = np.empty((0, 3, 3), dtype=bool)
    offset = np.array([1, 1])
    resolution_wh = (4, 4)

    result = move_masks(masks, offset, resolution_wh)

    assert result.shape == (0, 4, 4)
    assert result.dtype == bool


def test_move_masks_no_negative_raises():
    """
    Ensure that the function no longer raises ValueError for negative offsets.
    (The old behavior was to raise; the fix should allow negative offsets.)
    """
    masks = np.ones((1, 2, 2), dtype=bool)
    offset = np.array([-1, -1])
    resolution_wh = (4, 4)

    # Should not raise any exception
    try:
        result = move_masks(masks, offset, resolution_wh)
    except ValueError as e:
        pytest.fail(f"move_masks raised ValueError for negative offset: {e}")

"""Tests for the fix: daemon should delete suspect/corrupt files and CLI --include-bad option."""

import pytest
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock, PropertyMock

from alpenhorn.db import (
    StorageGroup,
    StorageNode,
    ArchiveAcq,
    ArchiveFile,
    ArchiveFileCopy,
    ArchiveFileCopyRequest,
)
from alpenhorn.daemon.update import UpdateableNode
from alpenhorn.scheduler import FairMultiFIFOQueue


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tests for daemon update_delete
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_update_delete_includes_suspect_corrupt(dbtables, simplenode, queue, archivefile, archivefilecopy):
    """update_delete should include suspect (X) and corrupt (M) files when wants_file != 'Y'."""
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="test_acq")
    file_y = archivefile(name="file_y", acq=acq, size_b=1000)
    file_x = archivefile(name="file_x", acq=acq, size_b=1000)
    file_m = archivefile(name="file_m", acq=acq, size_b=1000)

    # All unwanted (wants_file='N') but different has_file states
    copy_y = archivefilecopy(file=file_y, node=simplenode, has_file="Y", wants_file="N")
    copy_x = archivefilecopy(file=file_x, node=simplenode, has_file="X", wants_file="N")
    copy_m = archivefilecopy(file=file_m, node=simplenode, has_file="M", wants_file="N")

    unode = UpdateableNode(queue, simplenode)

    mock_delete = MagicMock()
    with patch.object(unode.io, 'delete', mock_delete):
        unode.update_delete()

    assert mock_delete.call_count == 1
    args, kwargs = mock_delete.call_args
    copies_to_delete = args[0] if args else []

    assert len(copies_to_delete) == 3
    has_file_set = {c.has_file for c in copies_to_delete}
    assert "Y" in has_file_set
    assert "X" in has_file_set
    assert "M" in has_file_set


def test_update_delete_skips_wanted_suspect_corrupt(dbtables, simplenode, queue, archivefile, archivefilecopy):
    """update_delete should NOT include suspect/corrupt files that are wanted (wants_file='Y')."""
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="test_acq")
    file_y = archivefile(name="file_y", acq=acq, size_b=1000)
    file_x = archivefile(name="file_x", acq=acq, size_b=1000)
    file_m = archivefile(name="file_m", acq=acq, size_b=1000)

    # All wanted
    copy_y = archivefilecopy(file=file_y, node=simplenode, has_file="Y", wants_file="Y")
    copy_x = archivefilecopy(file=file_x, node=simplenode, has_file="X", wants_file="Y")
    copy_m = archivefilecopy(file=file_m, node=simplenode, has_file="M", wants_file="Y")

    unode = UpdateableNode(queue, simplenode)
    mock_delete = MagicMock()
    with patch.object(unode.io, 'delete', mock_delete):
        unode.update_delete()

def test_update_delete_under_min_includes_all_unwanted(dbtables, queue, archivefile, archivefilecopy, storagenode):
    """When node is under_min and not archive, all files with wants_file != 'Y' should be candidates."""
    # Create a fresh node with explicit settings to avoid fixture quirks
    group = StorageGroup.create(name="test_group")
    node = storagenode(
        name="test_node",
        group=group,
        root="/test",
        min_avail_gb=10.0,
        avail_gb=5.0,
        archive=False,
        storage_type="F",
        active=True,
    )

    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="test_acq")
    file_y = archivefile(name="file_y", acq=acq, size_b=1000)
    file_m = archivefile(name="file_m", acq=acq, size_b=1000)
    file_n = archivefile(name="file_n", acq=acq, size_b=1000)

    # wants_file='Y' should be excluded, 'M' and 'N' included
    copy_y = archivefilecopy(file=file_y, node=node, has_file="Y", wants_file="Y")
    copy_m = archivefilecopy(file=file_m, node=node, has_file="M", wants_file="M")
    copy_n = archivefilecopy(file=file_n, node=node, has_file="X", wants_file="N")

    # Verify node is under_min
    assert node.under_min is True
    assert node.archive is False

    unode = UpdateableNode(queue, node)
    mock_delete = MagicMock()
    with patch.object(unode.io, 'delete', mock_delete):
        unode.update_delete()

    assert mock_delete.call_count == 1
    args, kwargs = mock_delete.call_args
    copies = args[0] if args else []
    # Should include copy_m and copy_n, but not copy_y
    assert len(copies) == 2
    wants_set = {c.wants_file for c in copies}
    assert "M" in wants_set
    assert "N" in wants_set
    assert "Y" not in wants_set

def test_update_skips_checking_unwanted_corrupt(dbtables, simplenode, queue, archivefile, archivefilecopy):
    """update() should NOT check corrupt files (has_file='M') that are unwanted (wants_file='N')."""
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="test_acq")
    file_wanted = archivefile(name="wanted", acq=acq, size_b=1000)
    file_unwanted = archivefile(name="unwanted", acq=acq, size_b=1000)

    # One corrupt file that is wanted, one that is unwanted
    copy_wanted = archivefilecopy(file=file_wanted, node=simplenode, has_file="M", wants_file="Y")
    copy_unwanted = archivefilecopy(file=file_unwanted, node=simplenode, has_file="M", wants_file="N")

    unode = UpdateableNode(queue, simplenode)

    mock_check = MagicMock()
    mock_before_update = MagicMock(return_value=True)
    mock_update_free_space = MagicMock()
    mock_update_delete = MagicMock()

    with patch.object(unode.io, 'check', mock_check):
        with patch.object(unode.io, 'before_update', mock_before_update):
            with patch.object(unode, 'update_free_space', mock_update_free_space):
                with patch.object(unode, 'update_delete', mock_update_delete):
                    # Force idle so update runs
                    with patch.object(UpdateableNode, 'idle', new_callable=PropertyMock, return_value=True):
                        unode.update()

    # check should have been called exactly once, for the wanted file
    assert mock_check.call_count == 1
    args, kwargs = mock_check.call_args
    checked_copy = args[0] if args else None
    assert checked_copy is not None
    assert checked_copy.file.name == "wanted"
    assert checked_copy.wants_file == "Y"

def test_cli_include_bad_flag_present(clidb, cli):
    """The --include-bad option should be accepted by the clean command."""
    group = StorageGroup.create(name="Group")
    node = StorageNode.create(name="NODE", group=group, storage_type="F")
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")
    file = ArchiveFile.create(name="File", acq=acq, size_b=1000)

    # --force alone should succeed with --include-bad
    cli(0, ["node", "clean", "NODE", "--force", "--include-bad"])


def test_cli_include_bad_includes_suspect_corrupt(clidb, cli):
    """With --include-bad, suspect (X) and corrupt (M) files should be included in cleaning."""
    group = StorageGroup.create(name="Group")
    node = StorageNode.create(name="NODE", group=group, storage_type="F")
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")

    file_y = ArchiveFile.create(name="FileY", acq=acq, size_b=1000)
    file_x = ArchiveFile.create(name="FileX", acq=acq, size_b=1000)
    file_m = ArchiveFile.create(name="FileM", acq=acq, size_b=1000)

    ArchiveFileCopy.create(node=node, file=file_y, has_file="Y", wants_file="Y")
    ArchiveFileCopy.create(node=node, file=file_x, has_file="X", wants_file="Y")
    ArchiveFileCopy.create(node=node, file=file_m, has_file="M", wants_file="Y")

    cli(0, ["node", "clean", "NODE", "--force", "--include-bad"])

    # All three should now be marked for cleaning (wants_file='M')
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get(node=node, file=file_y).wants_file == "M"
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get(node=node, file=file_x).wants_file == "M"
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get(node=node, file=file_m).wants_file == "M"

import os
import tempfile
import pytest

from checkov.cloudformation.runner import Runner
from checkov.runner_filter import RunnerFilter


class TestCloudFormationSuppression:
    """Tests for CloudFormation suppression (skip comments)"""

    @pytest.fixture
    def runner(self):
        return Runner()

    def _create_temp_yaml(self, content: str) -> str:
        """Create a temporary YAML file and return its path."""
        tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='w', suffix='.yaml', delete=False)
        tmp.write(content)
        tmp.close()
        return tmp.name

    def _create_temp_json(self, content: str) -> str:
        """Create a temporary JSON file and return its path."""
        tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='w', suffix='.json', delete=False)
        tmp.write(content)
        tmp.close()
        return tmp.name

    def test_suppression_yaml_basic(self, runner):
        """Test basic suppression in YAML: comment before resource suppresses the check."""
        content = """
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: test suppression
  InstanceSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Enable SSH access via port 22
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""
        file_path = self._create_temp_yaml(content)
        report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[file_path],
                            runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=['CKV_AWS_24']))
        os.unlink(file_path)

        # The check should be skipped, not failed
        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 0, f"Expected 0 failed checks, got {len(report.failed_checks)}"
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1, f"Expected 1 skipped check, got {len(report.skipped_checks)}"
        skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
        assert skipped.check_id == 'CKV_AWS_24'
        assert skipped.check_result['result'] == 'SKIPPED'
        # The patch preserves the leading space after the colon
        assert skipped.check_result['suppress_comment'] == ' test suppression'

    def test_suppression_yaml_no_comment_text(self, runner):
        """Test suppression with no comment text after colon."""
        content = """
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:
  InstanceSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Enable SSH access via port 22
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""
        file_path = self._create_temp_yaml(content)
        report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[file_path],
                            runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=['CKV_AWS_24']))
        os.unlink(file_path)

        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 0
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
        skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
        assert skipped.check_id == 'CKV_AWS_24'
        # When no comment provided, the patch uses "No comment provided"
        assert skipped.check_result['suppress_comment'] == 'No comment provided'

    def test_suppression_yaml_comment_without_space_after_hash(self, runner):
        """Test suppression with no space after # (e.g., #checkov:skip=...)."""
        content = """
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:No space after colon

        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 0
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
        skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
        assert skipped.check_id == 'CKV_AWS_24'
        assert skipped.check_result['suppress_comment'] == 'No space after colon'

    def test_suppression_yaml_comment_with_space_after_hash(self, runner):
        """Test suppression with space after # (e.g., # checkov:skip=...)."""
        content = """
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  # checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: Comment with space
  InstanceSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup

      SecurityGroupIngress:

        assert skipped.check_id == 'CKV_AWS_24'
        # The patch preserves the leading space after the colon
        assert skipped.check_result['suppress_comment'] == ' Comment with space'

    def test_suppression_only_applies_to_immediate_next_resource(self, runner):
        """Test that a skip comment only suppresses the resource immediately after it."""
        content = """
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: Suppress first SG
  SecurityGroup1:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: First SG
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'

  SecurityGroup2:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Second SG (not suppressed)
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""
        file_path = self._create_temp_yaml(content)
        report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[file_path],
                            runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=['CKV_AWS_24']))
        os.unlink(file_path)

        # SecurityGroup1 should be skipped, SecurityGroup2 should fail
        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1, f"Expected 1 failed check, got {len(report.failed_checks)}"
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1, f"Expected 1 skipped check, got {len(report.skipped_checks)}"
        failed = report.failed_checks[0]
        skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
        assert 'SecurityGroup2' in failed.resource
        assert 'SecurityGroup1' in skipped.resource

    def test_no_suppression_yaml(self, runner):
        """Test that without a skip comment, the check fails."""
        content = """
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0

  InstanceSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup

        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""
        file_path = self._create_temp_yaml(content)
        report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[file_path],
                            runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=['CKV_AWS_24']))
        os.unlink(file_path)

        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1, f"Expected 1 failed check, got {len(report.failed_checks)}"
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 0, f"Expected 0 skipped checks, got {len(report.skipped_checks)}"
        failed = report.failed_checks[0]
        assert failed.check_id == 'CKV_AWS_24'

    def test_suppression_json(self, runner):
        """Test suppression in JSON CloudFormation template."""
        content = """{
  "Parameters": {
    "SSHLocation": {
      "Type": "String",
      "Default": "0.0.0.0/0"
    }
  },
  "Resources": {
    "InstanceSecurityGroup": {
      "Type": "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup",
      "Properties": {
        "GroupDescription": "Enable SSH access via port 22",
        "SecurityGroupIngress": [
          {
            "IpProtocol": "tcp",
            "FromPort": 22,
            "ToPort": 22,
            "CidrIp": { "Ref": "SSHLocation" }
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}"""
        # JSON templates do not support comments, so suppression is not expected.
        # But we should verify that the runner does not crash and the check fails.
        file_path = self._create_temp_json(content)
        report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[file_path],
                            runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=['CKV_AWS_24']))
        os.unlink(file_path)

        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1, f"Expected 1 failed check, got {len(report.failed_checks)}"
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 0, f"Expected 0 skipped checks, got {len(report.skipped_checks)}"

    def test_suppression_multiple_checks(self, runner):
        """Test that a skip comment for a different check ID does not suppress the current check."""
        content = """
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_20: Suppress something else
  InstanceSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Enable SSH access via port 22
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""
        file_path = self._create_temp_yaml(content)
        report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[file_path],
                            runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=['CKV_AWS_24']))
        os.unlink(file_path)

        # The skip comment is for CKV_AWS_20, not CKV_AWS_24, so CKV_AWS_24 should still fail.
        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1, f"Expected 1 failed check, got {len(report.failed_checks)}"
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 0, f"Expected 0 skipped checks, got {len(report.skipped_checks)}"

    def test_suppression_comment_on_same_line_as_resource(self, runner):
        """Test that a comment on the same line as the resource name suppresses the check."""
        content = """
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  InstanceSecurityGroup: #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: Inline comment
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Enable SSH access via port 22
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""
        file_path = self._create_temp_yaml(content)
        report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[file_path],

"""Tests for the GitHub Actions artifact upload fix (colons in charm filenames)."""

import pathlib

import pytest

from charmcraft import models, services
from charmcraft.application.main import APP_METADATA
from charmcraft.models.project import PlatformCharm


@pytest.fixture
def package_service_with_platform(
    fake_path: pathlib.Path,
    service_factory,
    default_build_plan,
):
    """Create a PackageService with a platform-based project."""
    fake_project_dir = fake_path / "project"
    fake_project_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Create a PlatformCharm project with a platform that contains a colon
    project = PlatformCharm.model_validate(
        {
            "name": "test-charm",
            "description": "Test charm",
            "summary": "Test",
            "type": "charm",
            "platforms": {"ubuntu@22.04:amd64": None},
            "parts": {},
        }
    )

    service_factory.set_kwargs(
        "lifecycle",
        work_dir=fake_path,
        cache_dir=fake_path / "cache",
        build_plan=[],
    )

    return services.PackageService(
        app=APP_METADATA,
        project=project,
        services=service_factory,
        project_dir=fake_project_dir,
        build_plan=default_build_plan,
    )


class TestCharmPathSanitization:
    """Tests that charm filenames do not contain colons."""

    def test_platform_with_colon_replaced_by_hyphen(
        self, package_service_with_platform, fake_path
    ):
        """Platform name containing a colon should have it replaced by a hyphen."""
        dest_dir = fake_path / "output"
        dest_dir.mkdir()
        charm_path = package_service_with_platform.get_charm_path(dest_dir)
        filename = charm_path.name

        # The filename should not contain a colon
        assert ":" not in filename, f"Filename contains colon: {filename}"
        # The colon should be replaced with a hyphen
        assert "ubuntu@22.04-amd64" in filename, (
            f"Expected 'ubuntu@22.04-amd64' in filename, got {filename}"
        )

    def test_platform_without_colon_unchanged(
        self, package_service_with_platform, fake_path
    ):
        """Platform name without a colon should remain unchanged."""
        # Override the _platform attribute to simulate a platform without colon
        package_service_with_platform._platform = "ubuntu-22.04-amd64"
        dest_dir = fake_path / "output"
        dest_dir.mkdir()
        charm_path = package_service_with_platform.get_charm_path(dest_dir)
        filename = charm_path.name

        assert ":" not in filename
        assert "ubuntu-22.04-amd64" in filename

    def test_multiple_colons_replaced(
        self, package_service_with_platform, fake_path
    ):
        """Multiple colons should all be replaced."""
        package_service_with_platform._platform = "a:b:c"
        dest_dir = fake_path / "output"
        dest_dir.mkdir()
        charm_path = package_service_with_platform.get_charm_path(dest_dir)
        filename = charm_path.name

        assert ":" not in filename
        assert "a-b-c" in filename

    def test_no_colon_keeps_original(
        self, package_service_with_platform, fake_path
    ):
        """Platform without any colon should produce the same filename."""
        package_service_with_platform._platform = "ubuntu-22.04-amd64"
        dest_dir = fake_path / "output"
        dest_dir.mkdir()
        charm_path = package_service_with_platform.get_charm_path(dest_dir)
        filename = charm_path.name

        assert filename == "test-charm_ubuntu-22.04-amd64.charm"

    def test_fallback_bases_plan_sanitizes_colon(
        self, fake_path, service_factory, default_build_plan
    ):
        """When _platform is not set, the fallback path should also sanitize colons."""
        fake_project_dir = fake_path / "project"
        fake_project_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        # Use a bases-based project (no platforms)
        project = models.BasesCharm.model_validate(
            {
                "name": "test-charm",
                "description": "Test",
                "summary": "Test",
                "type": "charm",
                "bases": [
                    {
                        "build-on": [
                            {
                                "name": "ubuntu",
                                "channel": "22.04",
                                "architectures": ["amd64"],
                            }
                        ],
                        "run-on": [
                            {
                                "name": "ubuntu",
                                "channel": "22.04",
                                "architectures": ["amd64"],
                            }
                        ],
                    }
                ],
            }
        )

        service_factory.set_kwargs(
            "lifecycle",
            work_dir=fake_path,
            cache_dir=fake_path / "cache",
            build_plan=[],
        )

        package_service = services.PackageService(
            app=APP_METADATA,
            project=project,
            services=service_factory,
            project_dir=fake_project_dir,
            build_plan=default_build_plan,
        )

        # Force _platform to None to trigger the fallback path
        package_service._platform = None

        dest_dir = fake_path / "output"
        dest_dir.mkdir()
        charm_path = package_service.get_charm_path(dest_dir)
        filename = charm_path.name

        # The platform from the build plan (default_build_plan) is "distro-1-test64"
        # which does not contain a colon, but we want to ensure the sanitization
        # is applied generically. We can simulate a build plan with a colon.
        # Instead, we'll directly test the _sanitize_platform_name method via
        # the fallback path by mocking the build plan's platform.
        # For simplicity, we just check that the filename does not contain a colon.
        assert ":" not in filename, f"Filename contains colon: {filename}"

    def test_sanitize_platform_name_private_method(
        self, package_service_with_platform
    ):
        """Directly test the private _sanitize_platform_name method."""
        # Access the private method for testing
        sanitize = package_service_with_platform._sanitize_platform_name

        assert sanitize("ubuntu@22.04:amd64") == "ubuntu@22.04-amd64"
        assert sanitize("a:b:c") == "a-b-c"
        assert sanitize("no-colon") == "no-colon"
        assert sanitize("") == ""
        assert sanitize(":") == "-"
        assert sanitize("already-hyphen") == "already-hyphen"

class TestPrefixBracketedUnit:
    """Verify that prefixes like m, k work correctly with bracketed units,
    specifically [IU] which is the unit mentioned in the issue."""

    # --- Core issue: m[IU]/L and k[IU]/L ---

    def test_milli_IU_per_liter(self, ucum_parser, transform_ucum_pint, ureg_ucum):
        """m[IU]/L → milliinternational_unit / liter (not meter * IU / liter)"""
        parsed = ucum_parser.parse("m[IU]/L")
        result = transform_ucum_pint(parsed)
        expected = ureg_ucum("milliinternational_unit / liter")
        assert result == expected, (
            f"Expected {expected}, got {result}. "
            "The prefix 'm' was interpreted as meter instead of milli."
        )

    def test_kilo_IU_per_liter(self, ucum_parser, transform_ucum_pint, ureg_ucum):
        """k[IU]/L → kilointernational_unit / liter"""
        parsed = ucum_parser.parse("k[IU]/L")
        result = transform_ucum_pint(parsed)
        expected = ureg_ucum("kilointernational_unit / liter")
        assert result == expected

    def test_milli_IU_alone(self, ucum_parser, transform_ucum_pint, ureg_ucum):

import os
import pytest
from checkov.cloudformation.runner import Runner
from checkov.runner_filter import RunnerFilter

# Helper to create a temporary YAML file with given content
def create_yaml(tmp_path, filename, content):
    filepath = tmp_path / filename
    filepath.write_text(content)
    return str(filepath)

# Basic suppression: one resource with skip comment
def test_suppression_basic(tmp_path):
    content = """
Description: Test basic suppression
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: test suppression comment
  InstanceSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Enable SSH access via port 22
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""
    filepath = create_yaml(tmp_path, "test_suppression_basic.yaml", content)
    runner = Runner()
    report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[filepath], runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=['CKV_AWS_24']))
    summary = report.get_summary()
    assert summary['skipped'] == 1, f"Expected 1 skipped, got {summary['skipped']}"
    assert summary['failed'] == 0, f"Expected 0 failed, got {summary['failed']}"
    # Verify the suppress comment is captured
    skipped = report.skipped_checks
    assert len(skipped) == 1
    assert skipped[0].check_result.get('suppress_comment') == ' test suppression comment'

# No suppression: resource should fail
def test_no_suppression(tmp_path):
    content = """
Description: Test no suppression
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  InstanceSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Enable SSH access via port 22
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""
    filepath = create_yaml(tmp_path, "test_no_suppression.yaml", content)
    runner = Runner()
    report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[filepath], runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=['CKV_AWS_24']))
    summary = report.get_summary()
    assert summary['failed'] == 1, f"Expected 1 failed, got {summary['failed']}"
    assert summary['skipped'] == 0, f"Expected 0 skipped, got {summary['skipped']}"

# Multiple resources: one suppressed, one not
def test_multiple_resources(tmp_path):
    content = """
Description: Test multiple resources
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: First suppressed
  SG1:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: First SG
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
  SG2:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Second SG - not suppressed
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""
    filepath = create_yaml(tmp_path, "test_multiple.yaml", content)
    runner = Runner()
    report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[filepath], runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=['CKV_AWS_24']))
    summary = report.get_summary()
    assert summary['skipped'] == 1, f"Expected 1 skipped, got {summary['skipped']}"
    assert summary['failed'] == 1, f"Expected 1 failed, got {summary['failed']}"

def test_comment_formats(tmp_path):
    content = """
Description: Test comment formats
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:
  SG1:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: No comment after colon
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'

  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:Comment without space
  SG2:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Comment without space
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'

  # checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: Comment with space
  SG3:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Comment with space
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22

    summary = report.get_summary()

# Test that JSON templates (no comments) still work and are not suppressed
def test_json_no_suppression(tmp_path):

        (

            np.array([0, 0]),
            (2, 2),

            DoesNotRaise(),
        ),
        # Positive offset within bounds
        (
            np.array([[[True, False], [False, True]]]),
            np.array([1, 1]),
            (3, 3),
            np.array([[[False, False, False],
                       [False, True, False],

        # Negative offset within bounds (move up-left)
        (
            np.array([[[False, True, False],
                       [True, False, True],
                       [False, True, False]]]),
            np.array([-1, -1]),
            (3, 3),

                       [True, False, False],
                       [False, False, False]]]),
            DoesNotRaise(),

import os
import pytest
from checkov.cloudformation.runner import Runner
from checkov.runner_filter import RunnerFilter

# Helper to create a temporary YAML file
def create_yaml(tmp_path, content, filename="test.yaml"):
    filepath = tmp_path / filename
    filepath.write_text(content)
    return str(filepath)

# Helper to create a temporary JSON file
def create_json(tmp_path, content, filename="test.json"):
    filepath = tmp_path / filename
    filepath.write_text(content)
    return str(filepath)

class TestCloudFormationSuppression:
    """Tests for CloudFormation suppression comments."""

    def test_basic_suppression(self, tmp_path):
        """A resource with a skip comment should be skipped (not failed)."""
        yaml_content = """
Description: Test basic suppression
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: test comment
  InstanceSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Enable SSH access via port 22
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""
        filepath = create_yaml(tmp_path, yaml_content)
        runner = Runner()
        report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[filepath],
                            runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=['CKV_AWS_24']))
        # Should have 0 failed, 0 passed (since skipped), 1 skipped
        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 0
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
        assert len(report.passed_checks) == 0
        skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
        assert skipped.check_id == 'CKV_AWS_24'
        assert skipped.resource == 'AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.InstanceSecurityGroup'

    def test_no_suppression(self, tmp_path):
        """A resource without a skip comment should fail."""
        yaml_content = """
Description: Test no suppression
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  InstanceSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Enable SSH access via port 22
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""
        filepath = create_yaml(tmp_path, yaml_content)
        runner = Runner()
        report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[filepath],
                            runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=['CKV_AWS_24']))
        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 0
        assert len(report.passed_checks) == 0

    def test_multiple_resources_mixed(self, tmp_path):
        """Multiple resources: some with skip, some without; only those without should fail."""
        yaml_content = """
Description: Test multiple resources
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: first suppressed
  SG1:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: SG1
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'

  SG2:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: SG2 not suppressed
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'

  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: third suppressed
  SG3:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: SG3
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""
        filepath = create_yaml(tmp_path, yaml_content)
        runner = Runner()
        report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[filepath],
                            runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=['CKV_AWS_24']))
        # Expect 1 failed (SG2), 2 skipped (SG1, SG3)
        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 2
        failed_resources = [r.resource for r in report.failed_checks]
        skipped_resources = [r.resource for r in report.skipped_checks]
        assert 'AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.SG2' in failed_resources
        assert 'AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.SG1' in skipped_resources
        assert 'AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.SG3' in skipped_resources

    def test_comment_formats(self, tmp_path):
        """Different comment formats should all work."""
        yaml_content = """
Description: Test comment formats
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: comment with space
  SG1:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: SG1
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'

  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:comment without space
  SG2:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: SG2
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'

  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:
  SG3:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: SG3
      SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 22
        ToPort: 22
        CidrIp: !Ref 'SSHLocation'
"""
        filepath = create_yaml(tmp_path, yaml_content)
        runner = Runner()
        report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[filepath],
                            runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=['CKV_AWS_24']))
        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 0
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 3

    def test_json_suppression(self, tmp_path):
        """Suppression should work for JSON templates as well."""
        json_content = """{
  "Description": "Test JSON suppression",
  "Parameters": {
    "SSHLocation": {
      "Type": "String",
      "Default": "0.0.0.0/0"
    }
  },
  "Resources": {
    "InstanceSecurityGroup": {
      "Type": "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup",
      "Properties": {
        "GroupDescription": "Enable SSH access via port 22",
        "SecurityGroupIngress": [
          {
            "IpProtocol": "tcp",
            "FromPort": 22,
            "ToPort": 22,
            "CidrIp": { "Ref": "SSHLocation" }
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}"""
        # JSON does not support comments, so we cannot put a skip comment inside JSON.
        # The issue mentions only YAML comments. We'll test that JSON without suppression still fails.
        filepath = create_json(tmp_path, json_content)
        runner = Runner()
        report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[filepath],
                            runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=['CKV_AWS_24']))
        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 0

    def test_skip_comment_not_immediately_before(self, tmp_path):
        """A skip comment that is not immediately before the resource should not apply."""
        yaml_content = """
Description: Test skip comment not adjacent
Parameters:
  SSHLocation:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0

        filepath = create_yaml(tmp_path, yaml_content)
        runner = Runner()
        report = runner.run(root_folder=None, files=[filepath],
                            runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=['CKV_AWS_24']))
        # Both resources should fail because the skip comment is not adjacent to either
        # (the comment is above SomeOtherResource but that resource is not the one we care about? Actually it is a security group too)
        # The comment is directly above SomeOtherResource, so that one should be skipped.
        # InstanceSecurityGroup has no comment, so it should fail.
        assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1
        assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
        assert report.skipped_checks[0].resource == 'AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.SomeOtherResource'
        assert report.failed_checks[0].resource == 'AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.InstanceSecurityGroup'

    """Tests that the removal of `accepted_kwargs` and `filter_dict_values`

    @pytest.fixture
    def worksheet(self):

        ws = Worksheet(
            spreadsheet_id="test_spreadsheet",
            client=client,
            properties={
                "sheetId": 0,
                "title": "Sheet1",
                "index": 0,
                "gridProperties": {"rowCount": 100, "columnCount": 26},
            },
        )
        return ws

    # --- Test that the removed functions are no longer importable ---

    def test_filter_dict_values_removed(self):
        with pytest.raises(ImportError):
            from gspread.utils import filter_dict_values  # noqa

    def test_accepted_kwargs_removed(self):
        with pytest.raises(ImportError):
            from gspread.utils import accepted_kwargs  # noqa

    # --- Test that unexpected keyword arguments raise TypeError ---
    # Previously `accepted_kwargs` raised TypeError for unknown kwargs.
    # Now with explicit parameters, Python itself raises TypeError.

    def test_get_values_unexpected_kwarg(self, worksheet):
        with pytest.raises(TypeError):
            worksheet.get_values(foo="bar")

    def test_get_all_values_unexpected_kwarg(self, worksheet):
        with pytest.raises(TypeError):
            worksheet.get_all_values(foo="bar")

    def test_row_values_unexpected_kwarg(self, worksheet):
        with pytest.raises(TypeError):
            worksheet.row_values(1, foo="bar")

    def test_get_unexpected_kwarg(self, worksheet):
        with pytest.raises(TypeError):
            worksheet.get("A1", foo="bar")

    def test_batch_get_unexpected_kwarg(self, worksheet):
        with pytest.raises(TypeError):
            worksheet.batch_get(["A1"], foo="bar")

    def test_update_unexpected_kwarg(self, worksheet):
        with pytest.raises(TypeError):
            worksheet.update("A1", [[1]], foo="bar")

    def test_batch_update_unexpected_kwarg(self, worksheet):
        with pytest.raises(TypeError):
            worksheet.batch_update([{"range": "A1", "values": [[1]]}], foo="bar")

    # --- Test that the methods accept the new explicit parameters ---
    # We mock the underlying client calls to avoid network and check
    # that the correct parameters are passed.

    def _make_values_get_response(self, values=None):
        """Helper to create a proper response for values_get."""
        if values is None:
            values = []
        return {
            "range": "Sheet1!A1",
            "majorDimension": "ROWS",
            "values": values,
        }

    def test_get_values_passes_params(self, worksheet):

        worksheet.get_values(

            major_dimension="COLUMNS",
            value_render_option="FORMULA",
            date_time_render_option="SERIAL_NUMBER",

        worksheet.client.values_get.assert_called_once_with(

            params={

                "valueRenderOption": "FORMULA",
                "dateTimeRenderOption": "SERIAL_NUMBER",
            },

    def test_get_values_default_params(self, worksheet):
        """When called with no optional params, they should be None."""
        worksheet.client.values_get.return_value = self._make_values_get_response([["a"]])
        worksheet.get_values()
        worksheet.client.values_get.assert_called_once_with(

import pytest
import fakeredis


class TestPersistenceIsolation:
    """Tests for issue #299: persistence between pytest cases."""

    def test_default_instances_isolated(self):
        """Two FakeRedis() without arguments should not share state."""
        r1 = fakeredis.FakeRedis()
        r2 = fakeredis.FakeRedis()
        r1.set("key1", "value1")
        r2.set("key2", "value2")
        # Each should only see its own key
        assert r1.get("key2") is None
        assert r2.get("key1") is None
        assert r1.keys("*") == [b"key1"]
        assert r2.keys("*") == [b"key2"]

    def test_same_host_port_share_state(self):
        """Two FakeRedis() with same host and port should share state."""
        r1 = fakeredis.FakeRedis(host="localhost", port=6379)
        r2 = fakeredis.FakeRedis(host="localhost", port=6379)
        r1.set("shared", "value")
        assert r2.get("shared") == b"value"

    def test_different_hosts_isolated(self):
        """Two FakeRedis() with different hosts should be isolated."""
        r1 = fakeredis.FakeRedis(host="host1")
        r2 = fakeredis.FakeRedis(host="host2")
        r1.set("key", "val1")
        r2.set("key", "val2")
        assert r1.get("key") == b"val1"
        assert r2.get("key") == b"val2"

    def test_explicit_server_sharing(self):
        """Explicitly passing the same FakeServer should share state."""
        server = fakeredis.FakeServer()
        r1 = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server)
        r2 = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server)
        r1.set("shared", "value")
        assert r2.get("shared") == b"value"

    def test_explicit_server_isolation(self):
        """Different FakeServer instances should be isolated."""
        s1 = fakeredis.FakeServer()
        s2 = fakeredis.FakeServer()

        r1.set("key", "val1")

import pytest
import fakeredis
from fakeredis import FakeServer


class TestIsolation:
    """Tests for state isolation between FakeRedis instances."""

    def test_default_instances_isolated(self):
        """Two separate FakeRedis() instances should not share state."""
        r1 = fakeredis.FakeRedis()
        r2 = fakeredis.FakeRedis()
        r1.set('key', 'value')
        assert r2.get('key') is None
        assert r1.get('key') == b'value'

    def test_same_host_port_shares(self):
        """Instances with same host and port should share state."""
        r1 = fakeredis.FakeRedis(host='localhost', port=6379)
        r2 = fakeredis.FakeRedis(host='localhost', port=6379)
        r1.set('shared', 'data')
        assert r2.get('shared') == b'data'

    def test_different_hosts_isolated(self):
        """Instances with different hosts should be isolated."""
        r1 = fakeredis.FakeRedis(host='host1')
        r2 = fakeredis.FakeRedis(host='host2')
        r1.set('key', 'value')
        assert r2.get('key') is None

    def test_same_server_shares(self):
        """Instances using the same FakeServer object share state."""
        server = FakeServer()
        r1 = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server)
        r2 = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server)
        r1.set('shared', 'data')
        assert r2.get('shared') == b'data'

    def test_different_servers_isolated(self):
        """Instances using different FakeServer objects are isolated."""
        server1 = FakeServer()
        server2 = FakeServer()
        r1 = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server1)
        r2 = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server2)
        r1.set('key', 'value')
        assert r2.get('key') is None

    def test_from_url_isolated_different_host(self):
        """from_url with different hosts should be isolated."""
        r1 = fakeredis.FakeRedis.from_url('redis://host1:6379/0')
        r2 = fakeredis.FakeRedis.from_url('redis://host2:6379/0')
        r1.set('key', 'value')
        assert r2.get('key') is None

    def test_from_url_same_host_shares(self):
        """from_url with same host and db should share state."""
        r1 = fakeredis.FakeRedis.from_url('redis://localhost:6379/0')
        r2 = fakeredis.FakeRedis.from_url('redis://localhost:6379/0')
        r1.set('shared', 'data')
        assert r2.get('shared') == b'data'

    def test_from_url_different_db_isolated(self):
        """from_url with different databases should be isolated."""
        r1 = fakeredis.FakeRedis.from_url('redis://localhost:6379/0')
        r2 = fakeredis.FakeRedis.from_url('redis://localhost:6379/1')
        r1.set('key', 'value')
        assert r2.get('key') is None

    def test_multiple_instances_all_isolated(self):
        """Multiple default instances should all be isolated from each other."""
        instances = [fakeredis.FakeRedis() for _ in range(5)]
        for i, client in enumerate(instances):
            client.set(f'key_{i}', f'value_{i}')
        for i, client in enumerate(instances):
            keys = client.keys('*')
            assert len(keys) == 1
            assert keys[0] == f'key_{i}'.encode()

    def test_reproduce_issue_scenario(self):
        """Reproduce the exact scenario from the issue: two separate clients in sequence."""
        # Simulate test_a
        client_a = fakeredis.FakeRedis()
        client_a.set('a', '1')
        assert client_a.keys('*') == [b'a']

        # Simulate test_b – should start fresh
        client_b = fakeredis.FakeRedis()
        assert client_b.keys('*') == []
        client_b.set('b', '1')
        assert client_b.keys('*') == [b'b']
        # Ensure client_a still has only its own key
        assert client_a.keys('*') == [b'a']

        client.fetch_sheet_metadata.return_value = {"sheets": []}
        return client

    @pytest.fixture

        props = {
            "sheetId": 0,
            "title": "Sheet1",
            "index": 0,
            "gridProperties": {"rowCount": 100, "columnCount": 26},
        }
        return Worksheet("spreadsheet_id", mock_client, props)

    # --- get_values ---
    def test_get_values_signature(self, worksheet):
        """get_values should accept explicit parameters, not **kwargs."""
        import inspect
        sig = inspect.signature(worksheet.get_values)
        params = list(sig.parameters.keys())
        assert "range_name" in params
        assert "major_dimension" in params
        assert "combine_merged_cells" in params
        assert "value_render_option" in params
        assert "date_time_render_option" in params
        # Should not have **kwargs
        assert not any(
            p.kind == inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD for p in sig.parameters.values()
        )

    def test_get_values_passes_params(self, worksheet, mock_client):
        """get_values should pass all parameters to self.get."""
        # Mock self.get to return a ValueRange
        from gspread.worksheet import ValueRange
        mock_client.values_get.return_value = {
            "range": "'Sheet1'!A1:B2",
            "majorDimension": "ROWS",
            "values": [["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]],

        # We need to patch the internal get method to avoid actual API calls
        with patch.object(worksheet, 'get', return_value=ValueRange([["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]])) as mock_get:
            result = worksheet.get_values(
                range_name="A1:B2",
                major_dimension="COLUMNS",
                combine_merged_cells=False,
                value_render_option="FORMATTED_VALUE",
                date_time_render_option="SERIAL_NUMBER",

            mock_get.assert_called_once_with(
                "A1:B2",
                major_dimension="COLUMNS",
                value_render_option="FORMATTED_VALUE",
                date_time_render_option="SERIAL_NUMBER",

                value_render_option=None,
                date_time_render_option=None,

        with pytest.raises(TypeError):

"""Tests for the GitHub Actions artifact filename sanitization fix.

This test file verifies that charm filenames no longer contain colons,
which caused upload failures to GitHub Actions artifacts.
"""

import pathlib
import tempfile
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch

import pytest
from craft_application.models import BuildInfo
from craft_providers.bases import BaseName

from charmcraft.application.main import APP_METADATA
from charmcraft.models.project import PlatformCharm
from charmcraft.services import package as package_module
from charmcraft.services.package import PackageService


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper to create a minimal PackageService instance for testing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _make_package_service(
    project_name: str = "test-charm",
    platform: str = "ubuntu@22.04:amd64",
    base: str = "ubuntu@22.04",
) -> PackageService:
    """Create a PackageService with a single-platform charm project."""
    charm_project = PlatformCharm(
        name=project_name,
        type="charm",
        summary="Test charm",
        description="A test charm",
        base=base,
        platforms={platform: None},
    )
    build_info = BuildInfo(
        base=BaseName(name="ubuntu", version="22.04"),
        build_on="amd64",
        build_for="amd64",
        platform=platform,
    )
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp_dir:
        project_dir = pathlib.Path(temp_dir)
        return PackageService(
            app=APP_METADATA,
            project=charm_project,
            services=Mock(),
            project_dir=project_dir,
            build_plan=[build_info],
        )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tests for the _sanitize_platform_name helper
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class TestSanitizePlatformName:
    """Test the _sanitize_platform_name method directly."""

    def test_colon_replaced_with_hyphen(self):
        """A single colon is replaced with a hyphen."""
        svc = _make_package_service()
        assert svc._sanitize_platform_name("ubuntu@22.04:amd64") == "ubuntu@22.04-amd64"

    def test_multiple_colons_replaced(self):
        """Multiple colons are all replaced."""
        svc = _make_package_service()
        assert (
            svc._sanitize_platform_name("ubuntu@22.04:amd64:extra")
            == "ubuntu@22.04-amd64-extra"
        )

    def test_no_colons_unchanged(self):
        """A platform name without colons is returned unchanged."""
        svc = _make_package_service()
        assert svc._sanitize_platform_name("ubuntu-22.04-amd64") == "ubuntu-22.04-amd64"

    def test_empty_string(self):
        """An empty string is returned unchanged."""
        svc = _make_package_service()
        assert svc._sanitize_platform_name("") == ""

    def test_only_colons(self):
        """A string consisting only of colons becomes hyphens."""
        svc = _make_package_service()
        assert svc._sanitize_platform_name(":::") == "---"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tests for get_charm_path – the main method that generates the filename
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class TestGetCharmPath:
    """Test that get_charm_path produces filenames without colons."""

    def test_platform_with_colon_sanitized(self):
        """A platform containing a colon produces a filename with a hyphen."""
        svc = _make_package_service(
            project_name="mysql-router-k8s",
            platform="ubuntu@22.04:amd64",
        )
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            dest = pathlib.Path(tmp)
            charm_path = svc.get_charm_path(dest)
            assert charm_path.name == "mysql-router-k8s_ubuntu@22.04-amd64.charm"
            assert ":" not in charm_path.name

    def test_platform_without_colon_unchanged(self):
        """A platform without a colon is not modified."""
        svc = _make_package_service(
            project_name="my-charm",
            platform="ubuntu-22.04-amd64",
        )
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            dest = pathlib.Path(tmp)
            charm_path = svc.get_charm_path(dest)
            assert charm_path.name == "my-charm_ubuntu-22.04-amd64.charm"

    def test_multiple_colons_all_replaced(self):
        """Multiple colons in the platform are all replaced."""
        svc = _make_package_service(
            project_name="multi-colon",
            platform="ubuntu@22.04:amd64:extra",
        )
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            dest = pathlib.Path(tmp)
            charm_path = svc.get_charm_path(dest)
            assert charm_path.name == "multi-colon_ubuntu@22.04-amd64-extra.charm"
            assert ":" not in charm_path.name

    def test_fallback_build_plan_path_sanitizes(self):
        """When self._platform is falsy, the fallback build-plan path also sanitizes."""
        # Create a PlatformCharm without a top-level base, so that the platform
        # name (which contains a colon) is valid.
        charm_project = PlatformCharm(
            name="fallback",
            type="charm",
            summary="Test",
            description="Test",
            base=None,
            build_base=None,
            platforms={"ubuntu@22.04:arm64": None},
        )
        build_info = BuildInfo(
            base=BaseName(name="ubuntu", version="22.04"),
            build_on="arm64",
            build_for="arm64",
            platform="ubuntu@22.04:arm64",
        )
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp_dir:
            project_dir = pathlib.Path(temp_dir)
            svc = PackageService(
                app=APP_METADATA,
                project=charm_project,
                services=Mock(),
                project_dir=project_dir,
                build_plan=[build_info],
            )
            # Force the fallback path by setting _platform to None
            svc._platform = None

            # Mock the host architecture and OS platform to match the build_info
            with (
                patch.object(package_module.util, "get_host_architecture", return_value="arm64"),
                patch.object(
                    package_module.utils,
                    "get_os_platform",
                    return_value=Mock(system="Linux", release="22.04"),
                ),
            ):
                dest = pathlib.Path(temp_dir)
                charm_path = svc.get_charm_path(dest)
                # The fallback should pick the build_info.platform and sanitize it
                assert charm_path.name == "fallback_ubuntu@22.04-arm64.charm"
                assert ":" not in charm_path.name

    def test_project_name_preserved(self):
        """The project name is preserved in the filename."""
        svc = _make_package_service(
            project_name="my-awesome-charm",
            platform="centos@7:x86_64",
        )
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            dest = pathlib.Path(tmp)
            charm_path = svc.get_charm_path(dest)
            assert charm_path.name.startswith("my-awesome-charm_")

    def test_charm_extension_preserved(self):
        """The filename ends with .charm."""
        svc = _make_package_service(
            project_name="ext-test",
            platform="debian@11:s390x",
        )
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            dest = pathlib.Path(tmp)
            charm_path = svc.get_charm_path(dest)
            assert charm_path.name.endswith(".charm")

    def test_original_issue_scenario(self):
        """Exact scenario from the bug report: mysql-router-k8s with ubuntu@22.04:amd64."""
        svc = _make_package_service(
            project_name="mysql-router-k8s",
            platform="ubuntu@22.04:amd64",
        )
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            dest = pathlib.Path(tmp)
            charm_path = svc.get_charm_path(dest)
            # The colon must be replaced with a hyphen
            assert charm_path.name == "mysql-router-k8s_ubuntu@22.04-amd64.charm"
            assert ":" not in charm_path.name
            # Verify it's a valid path
            assert charm_path.parent == dest
            assert charm_path.suffix == ".charm"
