import shlex
import sys
import unittest

from streamlink_cli.output import PlayerOutput


class TestMpvTitleArgument(unittest.TestCase):
    """
    Test that mpv receives the --title argument in the correct format
    (--title=value) as required by mpv >= 0.31.1, while other players
    (vlc, potplayer) remain unaffected.
    """

    def _get_mpv_args(self, title):
        """Helper to create a PlayerOutput for mpv and return the argument list."""
        po = PlayerOutput(
            cmd="/usr/bin/mpv",
            args="{filename}",
            filename="-",
            title=title,
            quiet=False
        )
        po.player_name = "mpv"
        return po._create_arguments()

    def _get_vlc_args(self, title):
        """Helper to create a PlayerOutput for vlc and return the argument list."""
        po = PlayerOutput(
            cmd="/usr/bin/vlc",
            args="{filename}",
            filename="-",
            title=title,
            quiet=False
        )
        po.player_name = "vlc"
        return po._create_arguments()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # mpv: correct format (--title=value)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_mpv_title_simple(self):
        """Simple title without special characters."""
        args = self._get_mpv_args("My Stream")
        # Expect: --title='My Stream' (shlex.quote adds single quotes)
        self.assertIn("--title='My Stream'", args)

    def test_mpv_title_with_spaces(self):
        """Title with spaces."""
        args = self._get_mpv_args("Title with spaces")
        self.assertIn("--title='Title with spaces'", args)

    def test_mpv_title_with_single_quotes(self):
        """Title containing single quotes."""
        args = self._get_mpv_args("It's a title")
        # shlex.quote will escape the single quote: 'It'"'"'s a title'
        # The resulting argument should be --title='It'"'"'s a title'
        self.assertTrue(any(arg.startswith("--title=") for arg in args))
        title_arg = next(arg for arg in args if arg.startswith("--title="))
        # Verify it can be parsed back correctly
        parsed = shlex.split("mpv " + title_arg)
        self.assertEqual(len(parsed), 2)
        self.assertEqual(parsed[1], "--title=It's a title")

    def test_mpv_title_with_double_quotes(self):
        """Title containing double quotes."""
        args = self._get_mpv_args('Title with "double" quotes')
        self.assertTrue(any(arg.startswith("--title=") for arg in args))
        title_arg = next(arg for arg in args if arg.startswith("--title="))
        parsed = shlex.split("mpv " + title_arg)
        self.assertEqual(len(parsed), 2)
        self.assertEqual(parsed[1], '--title=Title with "double" quotes')

    def test_mpv_title_with_dollar_sign(self):
        """Title containing $ (mpv property expansion)."""
        args = self._get_mpv_args("Price: $10")
        # The _mpv_title_escape method replaces $ with $$, so the title becomes "Price: $$10"
        # Then shlex.quote will quote it.
        self.assertTrue(any(arg.startswith("--title=") for arg in args))
        title_arg = next(arg for arg in args if arg.startswith("--title="))
        # After escaping, the value should contain $$10
        self.assertIn("$$10", title_arg)

    def test_mpv_title_empty(self):
        """Empty title."""
        args = self._get_mpv_args("")
        self.assertIn("--title=''", args)

    def test_mpv_title_special_chars(self):
        """Title with various special characters."""
        args = self._get_mpv_args("Special !@#$%^&*()")
        self.assertTrue(any(arg.startswith("--title=") for arg in args))
        title_arg = next(arg for arg in args if arg.startswith("--title="))
        parsed = shlex.split("mpv " + title_arg)
        self.assertEqual(len(parsed), 2)
        # The value should be preserved after parsing
        self.assertIn("Special", parsed[1])

    def test_mpv_title_unicode(self):
        """Title with Unicode characters."""
        args = self._get_mpv_args("Tѥst Āuƭhǿr")
        self.assertTrue(any(arg.startswith("--title=") for arg in args))
        title_arg = next(arg for arg in args if arg.startswith("--title="))
        parsed = shlex.split("mpv " + title_arg)
        self.assertEqual(len(parsed), 2)
        self.assertIn("Tѥst", parsed[1])

    def test_mpv_title_backslash(self):
        """Title containing backslash (mpv escape sequences)."""
        args = self._get_mpv_args(r"\$> test")
        # _mpv_title_escape should handle this
        self.assertTrue(any(arg.startswith("--title=") for arg in args))
        title_arg = next(arg for arg in args if arg.startswith("--title="))
        # The escaped title should be "$> test" (since \$> becomes $>)
        # But shlex.quote will quote it
        parsed = shlex.split("mpv " + title_arg)
        self.assertEqual(len(parsed), 2)
        # After parsing, the value should be "--title=$> test"
        self.assertEqual(parsed[1], "--title=$> test")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # mpv: ensure old format is NOT used
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_mpv_not_using_separate_arguments(self):
        """mpv must NOT use --title and value as separate arguments."""
        args = self._get_mpv_args("Test")
        # The old format would have '--title' followed by 'Test' as separate elements
        # The new format has a single element '--title=Test' (or quoted)
        self.assertNotIn("--title", [arg for arg in args if arg == "--title"])
        # Also ensure there is exactly one argument starting with --title=
        title_args = [arg for arg in args if arg.startswith("--title=")]
        self.assertEqual(len(title_args), 1)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # vlc: must remain unchanged (separate arguments)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_vlc_uses_separate_arguments(self):
        """VLC must still use --input-title-format and value as separate arguments."""
        args = self._get_vlc_args("Test Title")
        self.assertIn("--input-title-format", args)
        idx = args.index("--input-title-format")
        self.assertEqual(args[idx + 1], "Test Title")

    def test_vlc_unicode(self):
        """VLC with Unicode title."""
        args = self._get_vlc_args("Tѥst Āuƭhǿr")
        self.assertIn("--input-title-format", args)
        idx = args.index("--input-title-format")
        self.assertEqual(args[idx + 1], "Tѥst Āuƭhǿr")

    def test_vlc_empty_title(self):
        """VLC with empty title."""
        args = self._get_vlc_args("")
        self.assertIn("--input-title-format", args)
        idx = args.index("--input-title-format")
        self.assertEqual(args[idx + 1], "")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Edge case: player_name not set (should not add any title args)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_no_player_name_no_title_args(self):
        """If player_name is None, no title arguments should be added."""
        po = PlayerOutput(
            cmd="/usr/bin/someplayer",
            args="{filename}",
            filename="-",
            title="Test",
            quiet=False
        )
        po.player_name = None
        args = po._create_arguments()
        # Should not contain --title or --input-title-format
        self.assertNotIn("--title", args)
        self.assertNotIn("--input-title-format", args)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Integration: verify that the generated command can be executed
    # (syntax check via shlex parsing)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_mpv_command_parsable(self):
        """The generated mpv command should be parseable by shlex."""
        titles = [
            "Simple",
            "With spaces",
            "With 'single' quotes",
            'With "double" quotes',
            "With $pecial",
            "With \\$ escape",
            "Unicode: Tѥst",
        ]
        for title in titles:
            with self.subTest(title=title):
                args = self._get_mpv_args(title)
                # On POSIX, args is a list; simulate the command string
                cmd_str = "mpv " + " ".join(shlex.quote(a) for a in args)
                try:
                    parsed = shlex.split(cmd_str)
                except Exception as e:
                    self.fail(f"Failed to parse command for title {title!r}: {e}")
                # The parsed command should contain the title argument
                title_args = [a for a in parsed if a.startswith("--title=")]
                self.assertEqual(len(title_args), 1,
                                 f"Expected exactly one --title= argument for title {title!r}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import pytest
from setuptools_scm import Configuration
from setuptools_scm.version import meta, format_version, ScmVersion
from setuptools_scm._entrypoints import _import_name, _looks_like_qualified_name


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper functions used as custom version schemes (qualified name targets)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def my_custom_scheme(version: ScmVersion) -> str:
    """A custom version scheme that prepends 'custom-'."""
    return f"custom-{version.tag}"


def another_scheme(version: ScmVersion) -> str:
    """Another custom scheme that includes distance."""
    return f"another-{version.tag}-{version.distance or 0}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tests for the helper functions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestImportName:
    def test_import_existing_function(self):
        """Import a function that exists in this module."""
        func = _import_name(f"{__name__}.my_custom_scheme")
        assert func is my_custom_scheme

    def test_import_nonexistent_module_raises(self):
        """Importing a non-existent module should raise ImportError."""
        with pytest.raises(ImportError):
            _import_name("nonexistent.module.func")

    def test_import_nonexistent_attribute_raises(self):
        """Importing an existing module but missing attribute should raise ImportError."""
        with pytest.raises(ImportError):
            _import_name(f"{__name__}.does_not_exist")

    def test_import_without_dot_raises(self):
        """A name without a dot should raise ImportError (ValueError inside)."""
        with pytest.raises(ImportError):
            _import_name("justaname")


class TestLooksLikeQualifiedName:
    def test_simple_qualified_name(self):
        assert _looks_like_qualified_name("module.func") is True

    def test_deep_qualified_name(self):
        assert _looks_like_qualified_name("a.b.c.func") is True

    def test_no_dot(self):
        assert _looks_like_qualified_name("entrypoint") is False

    def test_contains_space(self):
        assert _looks_like_qualified_name("mod ule.func") is False

    def test_contains_equals(self):
        assert _looks_like_qualified_name("mod=ule.func") is False

    def test_contains_colon(self):
        assert _looks_like_qualified_name("mod:ule.func") is False

    def test_single_component(self):
        assert _looks_like_qualified_name("only") is False

    def test_empty_string(self):
        assert _looks_like_qualified_name("") is False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Integration tests for version scheme resolution
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestQualifiedNameVersionScheme:
    """Test that qualified names work for version schemes."""

    def test_qualified_name_version_scheme(self):
        config = Configuration(
            version_scheme=f"{__name__}.my_custom_scheme",
            local_scheme="no-local-version"
        )
        version_obj = meta(
            tag="1.0.0",
            distance=5,
            node="abc123",
            dirty=False,
            config=config
        )
        result = format_version(version_obj, **{
            "version_scheme": f"{__name__}.my_custom_scheme",
            "local_scheme": "no-local-version"
        })
        assert result == "custom-1.0.0"

    def test_qualified_name_with_distance(self):
        config = Configuration(
            version_scheme=f"{__name__}.another_scheme",
            local_scheme="no-local-version"
        )
        version_obj = meta(
            tag="2.1.0",
            distance=3,
            node="def456",
            dirty=False,
            config=config
        )
        result = format_version(version_obj, **{
            "version_scheme": f"{__name__}.another_scheme",
            "local_scheme": "no-local-version"
        })
        assert result == "another-2.1.0-3"

    def test_qualified_name_no_distance(self):
        config = Configuration(
            version_scheme=f"{__name__}.another_scheme",
            local_scheme="no-local-version"
        )
        version_obj = meta(
            tag="3.0.0",
            distance=None,
            node="ghi789",
            dirty=False,
            config=config
        )
        result = format_version(version_obj, **{
            "version_scheme": f"{__name__}.another_scheme",
            "local_scheme": "no-local-version"
        })
        assert result == "another-3.0.0-0"


class TestBackwardCompatibilityEntryPoints:
    """Test that existing entry point names still work."""

    def test_builtin_entry_point(self):
        config = Configuration(
            version_scheme="guess-next-dev",
            local_scheme="no-local-version"
        )
        version_obj = meta(
            tag="1.0.0",
            distance=2,
            node="xyz789",
            dirty=False,
            config=config
        )
        result = format_version(version_obj, **{
            "version_scheme": "guess-next-dev",
            "local_scheme": "no-local-version"
        })
        assert result == "1.0.1.dev2"

    def test_nonexistent_entry_point_raises(self):
        """A non-existent entry point (no dots) should raise AssertionError."""
        config = Configuration(
            version_scheme="nonexistent-entry-point",
            local_scheme="no-local-version"
        )
        version_obj = meta(
            tag="1.0.0",
            distance=1,
            node="test123",
            dirty=False,
            config=config
        )
        with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
            format_version(version_obj, **{
                "version_scheme": "nonexistent-entry-point",
                "local_scheme": "no-local-version"
            })


class TestFallbackBehavior:
    """Test that invalid qualified names fall back to entry point behavior."""

    def test_invalid_qualified_name_falls_back_and_fails(self):
        """A qualified name that cannot be imported should fall back to entry point
        lookup, and if that also fails, raise AssertionError."""
        config = Configuration(
            version_scheme="invalid.module.name.function",
            local_scheme="no-local-version"
        )
        version_obj = meta(
            tag="1.0.0",
            distance=1,
            node="invalid123",
            dirty=False,
            config=config
        )
        with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
            format_version(version_obj, **{
                "version_scheme": "invalid.module.name.function",
                "local_scheme": "no-local-version"
            })

    def test_qualified_name_falls_back_to_existing_entry_point(self):
        """If a qualified name fails to import, but the string happens to match
        an existing entry point name, it should use that entry point.
        This is an edge case: 'guess-next-dev' has no dots, so it won't be
        treated as a qualified name. But if someone writes 'setuptools_scm.version.guess_next_dev'
        (which is a valid qualified name), it should import directly.
        We test that a valid qualified name works even if it matches an entry point name."""
        # Use a qualified name that points to a real function
        config = Configuration(
            version_scheme="setuptools_scm.version.guess_next_dev",
            local_scheme="no-local-version"
        )
        version_obj = meta(
            tag="1.0.0",
            distance=2,
            node="abc",
            dirty=False,
            config=config
        )
        result = format_version(version_obj, **{
            "version_scheme": "setuptools_scm.version.guess_next_dev",
            "local_scheme": "no-local-version"
        })
        assert result == "1.0.1.dev2"


class TestNonQualifiedStringStillUsesEntryPoints:
    """Test that strings without dots are treated as entry point names."""

    def test_no_dot_uses_entry_point(self):
        config = Configuration(
            version_scheme="nonexistent-entry-point",
            local_scheme="no-local-version"

import pytest
from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


class TestSyllableTokenizerPerformance:
    """Tests for the SyllableTokenizer performance fix (issue #??)."""

    def setup_method(self):
        self.tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    def test_vowels_unchanged_after_numbers(self):
        """Tokenizing numbers should not modify the vowels string."""
        original_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels
        # Tokenize numbers many times
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels, (
            "Vowels string changed after tokenizing numbers"
        )

    def test_vowels_unchanged_after_mixed(self):
        """Tokenizing mixed alphanumeric should not modify vowels."""
        original_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels
        for _ in range(50):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("abc123")
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("99test")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

    def test_vowels_unchanged_after_unknown_chars(self):
        """Tokenizing unknown characters (e.g., '@') should not modify vowels."""
        original_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels
        for _ in range(50):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("@#$%")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

    def test_numbers_tokenized_without_error(self):
        """Tokenizing numbers should run without error and return a list."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("123")
        assert isinstance(result, list)

    def test_mixed_alphanumeric_without_error(self):
        """Mixed alphanumeric tokens should be tokenized without error."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("test123")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert len(result) > 0

    def test_normal_words_still_work(self):
        """Standard syllabification should still work."""
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("justification") == [
            "jus",
            "ti",
            "fi",
            "ca",
            "tion",
        ]
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("hello") == ["hel", "lo"]
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("a") == ["a"]

    def test_empty_string(self):
        """Empty string should return an empty list or a list with empty string."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("")
        assert result == [] or result == [""]

    def test_punctuation(self):
        """Punctuation should be handled without errors."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize(".")
        assert result == ["."]

    def test_special_chars(self):
        """Special characters should be handled without errors."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("@#$%")
        assert isinstance(result, list)

    def test_no_quadratic_growth(self):
        """
        Performance should not degrade quadratically with repeated calls on numbers.
        We test that tokenizing numbers many times is not dramatically slower than
        tokenizing words many times. This is a heuristic check.
        """
        import time

        # Warm up
        t = SyllableTokenizer()
        for _ in range(10):
            t.tokenize("99")
            t.tokenize("hello")

        # Time tokenizing numbers
        t_num = SyllableTokenizer()
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(500):
            t_num.tokenize("99")
        num_time = time.perf_counter() - start

        # Time tokenizing words
        t_word = SyllableTokenizer()
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(500):
            t_word.tokenize("thisisanextremelylongword")
        word_time = time.perf_counter() - start

        # Numbers should not be more than, say, 5x slower than words.
        # In the fixed version, numbers are actually faster.
        ratio = num_time / word_time
        assert ratio < 5.0, (
            f"Numbers took {num_time:.3f}s vs words {word_time:.3f}s, "
            f"ratio {ratio:.1f}x – possible quadratic degradation"
        )

    def test_vowels_not_growing_across_calls(self):
        """Multiple tokenizations of numbers should not cause vowels to grow."""
        t = SyllableTokenizer()
        initial_len = len(t.vowels)
        for _ in range(100):
            t.tokenize("999")
        assert len(t.vowels) == initial_len

import sys
import types
from unittest.mock import patch

import pytest

from setuptools_scm._entrypoints import (
    _load_qualified_name,
    _iter_version_schemes,
    _get_ep,
)
from setuptools_scm.version import ScmVersion


# A dummy version scheme function for testing
def my_custom_scheme(version: ScmVersion) -> str:
    return "custom-version"


# Another dummy for fallback testing
def fallback_scheme(version: ScmVersion) -> str:
    return "fallback-version"


class TestLoadQualifiedName:
    def test_load_existing_function(self):
        """Qualified name pointing to a callable in an importable module."""
        # Use the test module itself as the module
        module_name = __name__
        func_name = "my_custom_scheme"
        qualified = f"{module_name}:{func_name}"
        loaded = _load_qualified_name(qualified)
        assert loaded is my_custom_scheme

    def test_load_nonexistent_module(self):
        """Qualified name with a module that cannot be imported returns None."""
        loaded = _load_qualified_name("nonexistent_module:some_func")
        assert loaded is None

    def test_load_nonexistent_attribute(self):
        """Qualified name with a missing attribute returns None."""
        loaded = _load_qualified_name(f"{__name__}:nonexistent_func")
        assert loaded is None

    def test_no_colon_returns_none(self):
        """String without colon is not a qualified name."""
        loaded = _load_qualified_name("just_a_name")
        assert loaded is None

    def test_empty_module_or_func_returns_none(self):
        """Empty parts after split return None."""
        assert _load_qualified_name(":func") is None
        assert _load_qualified_name("module:") is None

    def test_multiple_colons(self):
        """Only first colon is used; rest are part of the function name."""
        # This is not a valid qualified name, but we test that it doesn't crash
        # and returns None because the module likely doesn't exist.
        loaded = _load_qualified_name("mod:func:extra")
        assert loaded is None


class TestIterVersionSchemes:
    def test_qualified_name_used(self):
        """When scheme_value is a qualified name that resolves, it is used."""
        qualified = f"{__name__}:my_custom_scheme"
        schemes = list(_iter_version_schemes("some_entrypoint", qualified))
        assert len(schemes) == 1
        assert schemes[0] is my_custom_scheme

    def test_fallback_to_entrypoint_when_qualified_fails(self):
        """If qualified name fails, fall back to entry point."""
        # Patch _get_ep to return a known function
        with patch(
            "setuptools_scm._entrypoints._get_ep", return_value=fallback_scheme
        ) as mock_get_ep:
            schemes = list(
                _iter_version_schemes("test_group", "nonexistent:func")
            )
            assert len(schemes) == 1
            assert schemes[0] is fallback_scheme
            mock_get_ep.assert_called_once_with("test_group", "nonexistent:func")

    def test_both_fail_returns_empty(self):
        """When both qualified and entry point fail, no schemes are yielded."""
        with patch(
            "setuptools_scm._entrypoints._get_ep", return_value=None
        ) as mock_get_ep:
            schemes = list(
                _iter_version_schemes("test_group", "nonexistent:func")
            )
            assert len(schemes) == 0
            mock_get_ep.assert_called_once_with("test_group", "nonexistent:func")

    def test_qualified_name_takes_precedence(self):
        """Qualified name is tried before entry point, even if entry point exists."""
        # Patch _get_ep to return a different function, but qualified should win
        with patch(
            "setuptools_scm._entrypoints._get_ep", return_value=fallback_scheme
        ) as mock_get_ep:
            qualified = f"{__name__}:my_custom_scheme"
            schemes = list(
                _iter_version_schemes("test_group", qualified)
            )
            assert len(schemes) == 1
            assert schemes[0] is my_custom_scheme
            # _get_ep should not be called because qualified succeeded
            mock_get_ep.assert_not_called()

    def test_list_of_mixed_schemes(self):
        """When scheme_value is a list, each element is processed."""
        qualified = f"{__name__}:my_custom_scheme"
        with patch(
            "setuptools_scm._entrypoints._get_ep", return_value=fallback_scheme
        ) as mock_get_ep:
            schemes = list(
                _iter_version_schemes("test_group", [qualified, "other_entry"])
            )
            assert len(schemes) == 2
            assert schemes[0] is my_custom_scheme
            assert schemes[1] is fallback_scheme
            mock_get_ep.assert_called_once_with("test_group", "other_entry")

    def test_callable_directly(self):
        """If scheme_value is already a callable, it is yielded directly."""
        schemes = list(
            _iter_version_schemes("test_group", my_custom_scheme)
        )
        assert len(schemes) == 1
        assert schemes[0] is my_custom_scheme

    def test_deduplication(self):
        """Duplicate schemes are not yielded twice (same object in list)."""
        qualified = f"{__name__}:my_custom_scheme"
        # The list contains the same string twice and the same callable once.
        # The string is deduplicated by the _memo set, but the callable is different.
        schemes = list(
            _iter_version_schemes(
                "test_group", [qualified, qualified, my_custom_scheme]
            )
        )
        # Two distinct yields: one from the first qualified string, one from the callable.
        assert len(schemes) == 2
        assert schemes[0] is my_custom_scheme
        assert schemes[1] is my_custom_scheme

from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


class TestSyllableTokenizerFix:
    """Tests for the SyllableTokenizer performance fix (issue #???)."""

    @pytest.fixture
    def tokenizer(self):
        return SyllableTokenizer()

    def test_vowels_not_growing(self, tokenizer):
        """After many calls with numbers, self.vowels must remain unchanged."""
        original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels
        # Process many numeric tokens
        for _ in range(100):
            tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels, "vowels attribute grew!"

    def test_tokenize_basic(self, tokenizer):
        """Basic syllabification works (output may vary, but must join back)."""
        words = ["justification", "hello", "programming", "a", "bc"]
        for word in words:
            result = tokenizer.tokenize(word)
            assert isinstance(result, list)
            assert "".join(result) == word

    def test_tokenize_numbers(self, tokenizer):
        """Numbers are tokenized without error and join back."""
        numbers = ["99", "123", "0", "999999"]
        for num in numbers:
            result = tokenizer.tokenize(num)
            assert isinstance(result, list)
            assert "".join(result) == num

    def test_tokenize_mixed_alphanumeric(self, tokenizer):
        """Mixed tokens like 'test123' work."""
        mixed = ["test123", "hello99", "abc123xyz"]
        for token in mixed:
            result = tokenizer.tokenize(token)
            assert isinstance(result, list)
            assert "".join(result) == token

    def test_tokenize_empty_string(self, tokenizer):
        """Empty string returns [''] (current behavior)."""
        result = tokenizer.tokenize("")
        assert result == [""]

    def test_tokenize_punctuation(self, tokenizer):
        """Punctuation characters are returned as separate tokens."""
        result = tokenizer.tokenize(".")
        assert result == ["."]

    def test_tokenize_special_chars(self, tokenizer):
        """Special characters (non‑alphanumeric, non‑punctuation) are treated as vowels."""
        # They will generate a warning, which we suppress for this test
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            result = tokenizer.tokenize("@#$%")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert "".join(result) == "@#$%"

    def test_tokenize_no_vowels(self, tokenizer):
        """Tokens with no vowels (e.g., 'bc') are returned as a single syllable."""
        result = tokenizer.tokenize("bc")
        assert result == ["bc"]

    def test_tokenize_single_vowel(self, tokenizer):
        """Single vowel token returns itself."""
        result = tokenizer.tokenize("a")
        assert result == ["a"]

    def test_tokenize_mixed_case(self, tokenizer):
        """Mixed case tokens work (case is preserved)."""
        result = tokenizer.tokenize("Hello99World")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert "".join(result) == "Hello99World"

    def test_warning_on_unknown_char(self, tokenizer):
        """Unknown characters (e.g., digits) still produce a warning."""
        with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="Character not defined in sonority_hierarchy"):

        )
        # Ratio should be reasonable (e.g., less than 5x)

import pytest
from jwt.api_jwt import PyJWT
from jwt.exceptions import InvalidAudienceError, MissingRequiredClaimError


class TestAudienceNull:
    """Tests for handling of 'aud': null in JWT payload."""

    @pytest.fixture
    def jwt(self):
        return PyJWT()

    def test_aud_null_no_audience_provided(self, jwt):
        """When aud is null and no audience is specified, decoding should succeed."""
        payload = {"sub": "test", "aud": None}
        token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret")
        # No audience argument -> should not raise
        decoded = jwt.decode(token, "secret", algorithms=["HS256"])
        # The aud claim should be absent from the decoded payload (since it was null)
        assert "aud" not in decoded

    def test_aud_null_with_audience_provided(self, jwt):
        """When aud is null and an audience is specified, should raise MissingRequiredClaimError."""
        payload = {"sub": "test", "aud": None}
        token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret")
        with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc_info:
            jwt.decode(token, "secret", audience="my_audience", algorithms=["HS256"])
        assert exc_info.value.claim == "aud"

    def test_aud_null_with_audience_list_provided(self, jwt):
        """Same as above but audience is a list."""
        payload = {"sub": "test", "aud": None}
        token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret")
        with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc_info:
            jwt.decode(token, "secret", audience=["aud1", "aud2"], algorithms=["HS256"])
        assert exc_info.value.claim == "aud"

    def test_aud_null_verify_aud_disabled(self, jwt):
        """When verify_aud is disabled, aud null should not cause any error."""
        payload = {"sub": "test", "aud": None}
        token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret")
        decoded = jwt.decode(
            token,
            "secret",
            algorithms=["HS256"],
            options={"verify_aud": False},
        )
        assert "aud" not in decoded

    def test_aud_null_does_not_affect_other_claims(self, jwt):
        """Other claims should be preserved when aud is null."""
        payload = {"sub": "test", "iss": "me", "aud": None}
        token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret")
        decoded = jwt.decode(token, "secret", algorithms=["HS256"])
        assert decoded["sub"] == "test"
        assert decoded["iss"] == "me"
        assert "aud" not in decoded

    def test_normal_aud_still_works(self, jwt):
        """Non-null aud should still be validated normally."""
        payload = {"sub": "test", "aud": "correct_audience"}
        token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret")
        # Should succeed with matching audience
        decoded = jwt.decode(token, "secret", audience="correct_audience", algorithms=["HS256"])
        assert decoded["aud"] == "correct_audience"

        # Should fail with wrong audience
        with pytest.raises(InvalidAudienceError):
            jwt.decode(token, "secret", audience="wrong_audience", algorithms=["HS256"])

        # Should fail when no audience provided but aud present
        with pytest.raises(InvalidAudienceError):
            jwt.decode(token, "secret", algorithms=["HS256"])

    def test_aud_null_with_audience_none_explicit(self, jwt):
        """Explicit audience=None should behave like not providing audience."""
        payload = {"sub": "test", "aud": None}
        token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret")
        decoded = jwt.decode(token, "secret", audience=None, algorithms=["HS256"])
        assert "aud" not in decoded

    def test_aud_null_in_list_claim(self, jwt):
        """If aud is a list containing None, that's different; but we test null as value."""
        # This is not the same as {"aud": null}, but ensure no confusion.
        payload = {"sub": "test", "aud": ["valid", None]}
        token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret")
        # This should raise InvalidAudienceError because list contains non-string
        with pytest.raises(InvalidAudienceError) as exc_info:
            jwt.decode(token, "secret", audience="valid", algorithms=["HS256"])
        assert "Invalid claim format in token" in str(exc_info.value)

    def test_aud_null_required_claim(self, jwt):
        """If 'aud' is in require list and aud is null, it should be treated as missing."""
        payload = {"sub": "test", "aud": None}
        token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret")
        with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc_info:
            jwt.decode(
                token,
                "secret",
                algorithms=["HS256"],
                options={"require": ["aud"]},
            )
        assert exc_info.value.claim == "aud"

import pytest
from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


class TestSyllableTokenizerFix:
    """Tests for the SyllableTokenizer performance fix (issue #???)."""

    def setup_method(self):
        self.tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    def test_vowels_not_mutated_by_numbers(self):
        """Tokenizing numbers should not add digits to self.vowels."""
        original_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels, (
            "vowels attribute was mutated after tokenizing numbers"
        )

    def test_vowels_not_mutated_by_unknown_chars(self):
        """Tokenizing unknown characters should not add them to self.vowels."""
        original_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("@#$%")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels, (
            "vowels attribute was mutated after tokenizing special chars"
        )

    def test_vowels_not_mutated_by_mixed(self):
        """Tokenizing mixed alphanumeric strings should not mutate vowels."""
        original_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("test123")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels, (
            "vowels attribute was mutated after tokenizing mixed strings"
        )

    def test_basic_word_tokenization(self):
        """Standard word tokenization should still work correctly."""
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("justification") == [
            "jus", "ti", "fi", "ca", "tion"
        ]
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("hello") == ["hel", "lo"]
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("a") == ["a"]

    def test_number_tokenization(self):
        """Numbers should be tokenized without error (exact split not specified)."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert all(isinstance(s, str) for s in result)
        # The concatenation should equal the original input
        assert "".join(result) == "99"

        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("123")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert "".join(result) == "123"

        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("0")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert "".join(result) == "0"

    def test_mixed_alphanumeric(self):
        """Mixed strings should be tokenized without error."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("test123")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert "".join(result) == "test123"

    def test_empty_string(self):
        """Empty string should return a list (exact content not specified)."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("")
        assert isinstance(result, list)

    def test_punctuation_only(self):
        """Punctuation should be tokenized as separate syllables."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize(".")
        assert result == ["."]

    def test_special_chars(self):
        """Special characters should be handled without error."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("@#$%")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert "".join(result) == "@#$%"

    def test_performance_not_quadratic(self):
        """Tokenizing numbers should not be O(n^2) relative to words.
        We check that tokenizing a long digit string does not take
        disproportionately longer than a long word string.
        """
        import timeit

        # Use a moderate number of iterations to avoid long test times
        number = 100
        time_digits = timeit.timeit(
            't.tokenize("999999999")',
            setup="import nltk; t = nltk.SyllableTokenizer()",
            number=number,
        )
        time_word = timeit.timeit(
            't.tokenize("thisisanextremelylongword")',
            setup="import nltk; t = nltk.SyllableTokenizer()",
            number=number,
        )
        # The ratio should be small (not orders of magnitude larger).
        # A reasonable bound: digits should not be more than 10x slower than words.
        # In the fixed version, both are O(n) and digits are actually faster.
        ratio = time_digits / time_word
        assert ratio < 10, (
            f"Tokenizing digits is {ratio:.1f}x slower than words; "
            "likely quadratic behavior remains."
        )

    def test_vowels_stable_across_calls(self):
        """Repeated tokenization of the same number should not change vowels."""
        vowels_before = self.tokenizer.vowels
        for _ in range(50):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("12345")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == vowels_before

# Helper to create a temporary git repository with a custom version scheme

def temp_git_repo(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:

    # Tag to have a known version base

        from setuptools_scm.version import ScmVersion

        def my_version_scheme(version: ScmVersion) -> str:
            return "custom-{}.{}".format(version.tag, version.distance)

        def my_local_scheme(version: ScmVersion) -> str:
            return "local-{}".format(version.node or "clean")

    )
    return mod_dir

class TestLoadQualifiedName:
    def test_valid_qualified_name(self):
        """Load a function from an existing module."""
        # Use os.path.join as a known function
        func = _load_qualified_name("os.path:join")
        assert func is os.path.join

    def test_invalid_module(self):
        """Non-existent module returns None."""
        assert _load_qualified_name("nonexistent_module:func") is None

    def test_invalid_function(self):
        """Non-existent function in existing module returns None."""
        assert _load_qualified_name("os:nonexistent_func") is None

    def test_no_colon(self):
        """String without colon returns None (not a qualified name)."""
        assert _load_qualified_name("guess-next-dev") is None

    def test_empty_string(self):
        """Empty string returns None."""
        assert _load_qualified_name("") is None

    def test_colon_only(self):
        """Just ':' returns None."""
        assert _load_qualified_name(":") is None

    def test_missing_module(self):
        """':func' returns None."""
        assert _load_qualified_name(":func") is None

        assert _load_qualified_name("os:") is None

# Tests for _iter_version_schemes (unit)

class TestIterVersionSchemes:
    def test_qualified_name_loaded(self, custom_scheme_module):
        """Qualified name string yields the correct callable."""
        sys.path.insert(0, str(custom_scheme_module.parent))
        try:
            schemes = list(
                _iter_version_schemes(
                    "setuptools_scm.version_scheme",
                    "myschemes.schemes:my_version_scheme",
                )
            )
        finally:
            sys.path.pop(0)
        assert len(schemes) == 1
        # Call it with a dummy version to verify it's the right function
        config = Mock()
        dummy_version = ScmVersion("1.0.0", distance=0, node=None, config=config)
        result = schemes[0](dummy_version)
        assert result == "custom-1.0.0.0"

    def test_fallback_to_entry_point(self, mocker):
        """When qualified name fails, fall back to entry point."""
        # Mock _get_ep to return a dummy callable
        dummy_func = lambda v: "from_ep"
        mocker.patch(
            "setuptools_scm._entrypoints._get_ep",
            return_value=dummy_func,
        )
        schemes = list(
            _iter_version_schemes(
                "setuptools_scm.version_scheme",
                "nonexistent:func",
            )
        )
        assert len(schemes) == 1
        assert schemes[0] is dummy_func

    def test_builtin_entry_point(self):
        """Built-in entry point name still works."""
        schemes = list(
            _iter_version_schemes(
                "setuptools_scm.version_scheme",
                "guess-next-dev",
            )
        )
        assert len(schemes) == 1
        # Verify it's callable and returns something
        config = Mock()
        dummy_version = ScmVersion("1.0.0", distance=0, node=None, config=config)
        result = schemes[0](dummy_version)
        assert isinstance(result, str)

    def test_list_of_schemes(self):
        """List of scheme strings (qualified and entry point) works."""
        # We'll use a mix: one qualified (os.path:basename) and one entry point
        schemes = list(
            _iter_version_schemes(
                "setuptools_scm.version_scheme",
                ["os.path:basename", "guess-next-dev"],
            )
        )
        assert len(schemes) == 2
        # First should be os.path.basename
        assert schemes[0] is os.path.basename
        # Second should be callable
        assert callable(schemes[1])

class TestGetVersionWithQualifiedName:
    def test_version_scheme_qualified(self, temp_git_repo, custom_scheme_module):
        """get_version uses qualified name for version_scheme."""
        sys.path.insert(0, str(custom_scheme_module.parent))
        try:
            version = get_version(
                root=str(temp_git_repo),
                version_scheme="myschemes.schemes:my_version_scheme",
            )
        finally:
            sys.path.pop(0)
        # The custom scheme returns "custom-{tag}.{distance}".  distance may be None
        # when the tag is exactly on the commit, so we accept either.
        assert version.startswith("custom-1.0.0.")

    def test_local_scheme_qualified(self, temp_git_repo, custom_scheme_module):
        """get_version uses qualified name for local_scheme."""
        sys.path.insert(0, str(custom_scheme_module.parent))
        try:
            version = get_version(
                root=str(temp_git_repo),
                version_scheme="guess-next-dev",
                local_scheme="myschemes.schemes:my_local_scheme",
            )
        finally:
            sys.path.pop(0)
        # The local scheme returns "local-{node}".  The version string should contain it.
        assert "local-" in version

    def test_invalid_qualified_name_raises(self, temp_git_repo):
        """Invalid qualified name (no fallback) raises error."""

        try:
            version = get_version(
                root=str(temp_git_repo),
                version_scheme=["myschemes.schemes:my_version_scheme", "guess-next-dev"],
            )
        finally:
            sys.path.pop(0)
        # First scheme returns "custom-{tag}.{distance}".  distance may be None.
        assert version.startswith("custom-1.0.0.")

import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch

from streamlink_cli.output import PlayerOutput


class TestMpvTitleSyntax(unittest.TestCase):
    """Tests that mpv receives --title=<value> (equals syntax) as required by mpv >= 0.31.1"""

    def setUp(self):
        # Default to POSIX behaviour for most tests
        self.patcher = patch("streamlink_cli.output.is_win32", False)
        self.patcher.start()
        self.addCleanup(self.patcher.stop)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: create a PlayerOutput and force player_name to "mpv"
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _mpv_args(self, title, player_cmd="/usr/bin/mpv"):
        po = PlayerOutput(cmd=player_cmd, title=title, args="-")
        po.player_name = "mpv"
        return po._create_arguments()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # mpv: title must be passed as --title=<value>
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def test_mpv_title_equals_syntax(self):
        args = self._mpv_args("Test Title")
        self.assertIn("--title=Test Title", args)

    def test_mpv_title_with_spaces(self):
        args = self._mpv_args("My Stream")
        self.assertIn("--title=My Stream", args)

    def test_mpv_title_with_special_chars(self):
        args = self._mpv_args("Title with 'quotes' and \"double\"")
        self.assertIn("--title=Title with 'quotes' and \"double\"", args)

    def test_mpv_title_empty_string(self):
        args = self._mpv_args("")
        self.assertIn("--title=", args)

    def test_mpv_title_none(self):
        po = PlayerOutput(cmd="/usr/bin/mpv", title=None, args="-")
        po.player_name = "mpv"
        args = po._create_arguments()
        self.assertNotIn("--title", args)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # mpv: dollar signs must be escaped (property expansion)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def test_mpv_title_dollar_escaped(self):
        args = self._mpv_args("$100")
        self.assertIn("--title=$$100", args)

    def test_mpv_title_escape_sequence(self):
        # \$> disables property expansion, so the title becomes "$> test"
        args = self._mpv_args(r"\$> test")
        self.assertIn("--title=$> test", args)

    def test_mpv_title_multiple_dollars(self):
        args = self._mpv_args("$$$")
        # Each $ becomes $$, so $$$ becomes $$$$$$
        self.assertIn("--title=$$$$$$", args)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # vlc must still use separate argument syntax (not affected)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def test_vlc_title_separate(self):
        po = PlayerOutput(cmd="/usr/bin/vlc", title="Test Title", args="-")
        po.player_name = "vlc"
        args = po._create_arguments()
        self.assertIn("--input-title-format", args)
        self.assertIn("Test Title", args)
        self.assertNotIn("--input-title-format=Test Title", args)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Windows: the command line string must contain --title=<value>
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def test_mpv_title_windows(self):
        with patch("streamlink_cli.output.is_win32", True):
            po = PlayerOutput(cmd="mpv.exe", title="Test Title", args="-")
            po.player_name = "mpv"
            cmdline = po._create_arguments()
            # On Windows _create_arguments returns a string
            self.assertIn("--title=Test Title", cmdline)
            # Ensure the old separate-argument form is not present
            self.assertNotIn('--title "Test Title"', cmdline)

    def test_mpv_title_windows_with_spaces(self):
        with patch("streamlink_cli.output.is_win32", True):
            po = PlayerOutput(cmd="mpv.exe", title="My Stream", args="-")
            po.player_name = "mpv"
            cmdline = po._create_arguments()
            # The equals sign must be present; quoting is handled by list2cmdline
            self.assertIn("--title=My Stream", cmdline)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Regression: ensure the fix does not break potplayer (separate logic)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def test_potplayer_title(self):
        # PotPlayer uses a backslash separator at the end of the URL.
        # This logic is Windows-specific, so we must simulate Windows.
        with patch("streamlink_cli.output.is_win32", True):
            po = PlayerOutput(
                cmd="potplayer.exe",
                title="Test Title",
                args="{filename}",
                filename="http://example.com/stream"
            )
            po.player_name = "potplayer"
            cmdline = po._create_arguments()
            # On Windows, _create_arguments returns a string.
            # The potplayer logic removes the last character of the filename,
            # appends backslash + title, then appends the last character again.
            # So "http://example.com/stream" becomes
            # "http://example.com/strea\Test Titlem"
            # The backslash is a single backslash (escaped in the string).
            expected = "http://example.com/strea\\Test Titlem"
            self.assertIn(expected, cmdline)

from jwt.exceptions import InvalidAudienceError, MissingRequiredClaimError


class TestAudienceNull:
    """Tests for handling of 'aud': null in JWT payload."""

    def test_aud_null_no_audience_specified(self):
        """When aud is null and no audience is specified, decode should succeed."""
        payload = {"some": "claim", "aud": None}
        token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret", algorithm="HS256")
        # Should not raise any audience-related error
        decoded = jwt.decode(token, "secret", algorithms=["HS256"])
        assert decoded["some"] == "claim"
        # aud may be present as None in decoded payload (since we didn't remove it)

import time
import pytest
from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


class TestSyllableTokenizerPerformance:
    """Tests for the SyllableTokenizer performance fix (issue #...)."""

    def setup_method(self):
        self.tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    def test_basic_functionality(self):
        """Basic tokenization still works."""
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("justification") == [
            "jus",
            "ti",
            "fi",
            "ca",
            "tion",
        ]
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("hello") == ["hel", "lo"]
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("a") == ["a"]
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("bc") == ["bc"]  # no vowels

    def test_numbers_tokenization(self):
        """Numbers are tokenized (result concatenates to original)."""
        for num in ["99", "123", "0", "456"]:
            result = self.tokenizer.tokenize(num)
            assert "".join(result) == num, (
                f"Tokenization of {num!r} produced {result!r}, "
                f"which does not concatenate back to {num!r}"
            )

    def test_mixed_alphanumeric(self):
        """Mixed alphanumeric strings are handled (result concatenates to original)."""
        for token in ["test123", "abc123", "xyz789", "456def"]:
            result = self.tokenizer.tokenize(token)
            assert "".join(result) == token, (
                f"Tokenization of {token!r} produced {result!r}, "
                f"which does not concatenate back to {token!r}"
            )

    def test_vowels_unchanged_after_numeric_calls(self):
        """The vowels attribute must not grow after tokenizing numbers."""
        original_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels, (
            f"Vowels changed from {original_vowels!r} to {self.tokenizer.vowels!r}"
        )

    def test_vowels_unchanged_after_mixed_calls(self):
        """Vowels must not grow after tokenizing various unknown characters."""
        original_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels
        for token in ["99", "123", "abc123", "xyz789", "456def"]:
            self.tokenizer.tokenize(token)
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

    def test_no_quadratic_behavior_on_numbers(self):
        """
        Tokenizing a long number string should not be disproportionately slower
        than a short one. This checks that the algorithm is not O(n²).
        """
        short = "9"
        long_ = "9" * 100  # 100 times longer

        # Warm up
        self.tokenizer.tokenize(short)
        self.tokenizer.tokenize(long_)

        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize(short)
        t_short = time.perf_counter() - t0

        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize(long_)
        t_long = time.perf_counter() - t0

        # If the algorithm were O(n²), the long token would take ~10000 times longer.
        # With O(n), it should take ~100 times longer.
        # Allow some tolerance for overhead.
        ratio = t_long / t_short if t_short > 0 else float("inf")
        # The long token is 100x the length, so O(n) would give ratio ~100.
        # O(n²) would give ratio ~10000. We set a generous upper bound.
        assert ratio < 500, (
            f"Long token took {ratio:.1f}x longer than short token, "
            f"suggesting quadratic behavior. Short: {t_short:.4f}s, Long: {t_long:.4f}s"
        )

    def test_edge_cases(self):
        """Edge cases like empty string, punctuation, special chars."""
        # Empty string
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("")
        assert result == [""] or result == []  # depends on implementation

        # Punctuation
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize(".")
        assert result == ["."]

        # Special characters (not in hierarchy)
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("@#$%")
        # They should be treated as vowels and not crash
        assert "".join(result) == "@#$%"

    def test_repeated_calls_no_performance_degradation(self):
        """
        Repeated calls with numbers should not become slower over time
        (the original bug caused quadratic slowdown as vowels grew).
        """
        # Measure time for first batch
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        t_first = time.perf_counter() - t0

        # Do many more calls to potentially trigger growth
        for _ in range(1000):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")

        # Measure time for second batch
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        t_second = time.perf_counter() - t0

        # The second batch should not be significantly slower than the first.
        # Allow some variance, but not orders of magnitude.
        ratio = t_second / t_first if t_first > 0 else float("inf")
        assert ratio < 5, (
            f"Second batch was {ratio:.1f}x slower than first, "
            f"indicating performance degradation. First: {t_first:.4f}s, Second: {t_second:.4f}s"
        )

from setuptools_scm._entrypoints import _load_qualified_name, _iter_version_schemes
from setuptools_scm import get_version
from setuptools_scm.version import ScmVersion, guess_next_dev_version


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tests for _load_qualified_name
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_load_qualified_name_valid():
    """A valid qualified name (module:function) should return the function."""
    func = _load_qualified_name("setuptools_scm.version:guess_next_dev_version")
    assert func is guess_next_dev_version


def test_load_qualified_name_no_colon():
    """A string without a colon should return None."""
    assert _load_qualified_name("guess-next-dev") is None


def test_load_qualified_name_empty_module():
    """Empty module part should return None."""
    assert _load_qualified_name(":func") is None


def test_load_qualified_name_empty_function():
    """Empty function part should return None."""
    assert _load_qualified_name("module:") is None


def test_load_qualified_name_nonexistent_module():
    """Non-existent module should return None."""
    assert _load_qualified_name("nonexistent_module:func") is None


def test_load_qualified_name_nonexistent_function():
    """Existing module but missing function should return None."""
    assert _load_qualified_name("setuptools_scm.version:does_not_exist") is None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tests for _iter_version_schemes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_iter_version_schemes_qualified_name():
    """A qualified name string should be loaded and yielded."""
    schemes = list(
        _iter_version_schemes(
            "setuptools_scm.version_scheme",
            "setuptools_scm.version:guess_next_dev_version",
        )
    )
    assert len(schemes) == 1
    assert schemes[0] is guess_next_dev_version


def test_iter_version_schemes_fallback_to_entrypoint():
    """When qualified name fails, fall back to entry point."""
    # "guess-next-dev" is a built-in entry point
    schemes = list(
        _iter_version_schemes(
            "setuptools_scm.version_scheme",
            "guess-next-dev",
        )
    )
    assert len(schemes) == 1
    # The returned callable should be the entry point's function
    assert schemes[0] is guess_next_dev_version


def test_iter_version_schemes_list_with_qualified_name():
    """A list containing a qualified name should work."""
    schemes = list(
        _iter_version_schemes(
            "setuptools_scm.version_scheme",
            ["setuptools_scm.version:guess_next_dev_version", "guess-next-dev"],
        )
    )
    assert len(schemes) == 2
    assert schemes[0] is guess_next_dev_version
    assert schemes[1] is guess_next_dev_version

def test_get_version_with_qualified_scheme(

        )
        args = po._create_arguments()

        assert len(title_args) == 1

        title_args = [a for a in args if a.startswith("--title")]
        assert len(title_args) == 1

        title_args = [a for a in args if a.startswith("--title")]

import timeit
from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


def test_vowels_not_growing():
    """The root cause of the performance issue was that self.vowels grew
    each time an unknown character (like a digit) was tokenized.
    After the fix, self.vowels must remain unchanged."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels  # string, not a list/set

    # Tokenize many different numbers (each digit is unknown)
    for _ in range(100):
        tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        tokenizer.tokenize("123")
        tokenizer.tokenize("456789")

    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels, (
        "self.vowels should not grow after tokenizing numbers"
    )


def test_basic_functionality():
    """Basic syllabification still works."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    # From the docstring
    result = tokenizer.tokenize("justification")
    assert isinstance(result, list)
    assert len(result) > 0
    assert "".join(result) == "justification"

    result = tokenizer.tokenize("hello")
    assert "".join(result) == "hello"

    result = tokenizer.tokenize("a")
    assert result == ["a"]


def test_numbers_return_whole():
    """Numbers (no vowels) should be returned as a single token.
    The vowel count check must use the original vowels, not the expanded set,
    otherwise digits (treated as vowels temporarily) would cause syllabification."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("123") == ["123"]
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("0") == ["0"]


def test_mixed_alphanumeric():
    """Mixed tokens should be handled without error."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    result = tokenizer.tokenize("test123")
    assert isinstance(result, list)
    assert "".join(result) == "test123"

    result = tokenizer.tokenize("abc99xyz")
    assert "".join(result) == "abc99xyz"


def test_empty_string():
    """Empty string should not crash."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    result = tokenizer.tokenize("")
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_punctuation():
    """Punctuation should be handled gracefully."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    result = tokenizer.tokenize(".")
    assert result == ["."]

    assert "".join(result) == "!?"

import sys
import types
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator

import pytest

from setuptools_scm._entrypoints import (
    _call_version_scheme,
    _iter_version_schemes,
    _load_qualified_name,
)
from setuptools_scm.version import ScmVersion


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: a dummy version object that satisfies the ScmVersion protocol
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class DummyVersion:
    def __init__(self, tag: str = "1.0.0") -> None:
        self.tag = tag
        self.exact = True
        self.distance = 0
        self.node = None
        self.dirty = False
        self.branch = None
        self.version = tag
        self.prefix = ""
        self.suffix = ""
        self.time = None

    def format_with(self, fmt: str) -> str:
        # Mimic the real ScmVersion.format_with which passes the tag as a
        # keyword argument so that "{tag}" in the format string works.
        return fmt.format(tag=self.tag)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: a simple version scheme function we can reference by qualified name
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def my_custom_scheme(version: ScmVersion) -> str:
    return f"custom-{version.tag}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tests for _load_qualified_name
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class TestLoadQualifiedName:
    def test_load_existing_function(self) -> None:
        """A valid 'module:function' string loads the callable."""
        qn = f"{__name__}:my_custom_scheme"
        func = _load_qualified_name(qn)
        assert func is not None
        assert callable(func)
        assert func is my_custom_scheme

    def test_load_builtin_function(self) -> None:
        """Built‑in module functions can be loaded."""
        qn = "os.path:basename"
        func = _load_qualified_name(qn)
        assert func is not None
        assert callable(func)
        assert func("/a/b") == "b"

    def test_missing_colon_returns_none(self) -> None:
        """A string without ':' is not a qualified name."""
        assert _load_qualified_name("just_a_name") is None

    def test_empty_module_returns_none(self) -> None:
        """Empty module part yields None."""
        assert _load_qualified_name(":func") is None

    def test_empty_function_returns_none(self) -> None:
        """Empty function part yields None."""
        assert _load_qualified_name("module:") is None

    def test_nonexistent_module_returns_none(self) -> None:
        """ImportError is caught and None is returned."""
        assert _load_qualified_name("does_not_exist_xyz:func") is None

    def test_nonexistent_attribute_returns_none(self) -> None:
        """AttributeError is caught and None is returned."""
        assert _load_qualified_name("os.path:does_not_exist") is None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tests for _iter_version_schemes with qualified names
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class TestIterVersionSchemesQualified:
    def test_qualified_name_yields_function(self) -> None:
        """A qualified name is resolved and yielded."""
        qn = f"{__name__}:my_custom_scheme"
        schemes = list(_iter_version_schemes("test_ep", qn))
        assert len(schemes) == 1
        assert callable(schemes[0])
        assert schemes[0] is my_custom_scheme

    def test_qualified_name_result_called(self) -> None:
        """The yielded function can be called and returns the expected string."""
        qn = f"{__name__}:my_custom_scheme"
        scheme = next(_iter_version_schemes("test_ep", qn))
        ver = DummyVersion("2.0.0")
        assert scheme(ver) == "custom-2.0.0"

    def test_fallback_to_entry_point_when_qualified_name_fails(self) -> None:
        """If the qualified name cannot be loaded, the entry point is tried."""
        # Use a name that is not a valid qualified name (no colon) but is a
        # known entry point.  "guess_next_version" is a built‑in scheme.
        schemes = list(_iter_version_schemes("setuptools_scm.version_scheme", "guess-next-dev"))
        assert len(schemes) >= 1
        assert callable(schemes[0])

    def test_qualified_name_takes_precedence_over_entry_point(self) -> None:
        """A valid qualified name is used even if an entry point with the same
        name exists."""
        # We cannot easily guarantee an entry point with the same name,
        # but we can verify that the qualified name path is tried first.
        qn = f"{__name__}:my_custom_scheme"
        schemes = list(_iter_version_schemes("setuptools_scm.version_scheme", qn))
        assert len(schemes) == 1
        assert schemes[0] is my_custom_scheme


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tests for _call_version_scheme with qualified names
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class TestCallVersionSchemeQualified:
    def test_qualified_name_returns_result(self) -> None:
        """_call_version_scheme uses the qualified name and returns the
        scheme's output."""
        qn = f"{__name__}:my_custom_scheme"
        ver = DummyVersion("3.0.0")
        result = _call_version_scheme(ver, "test_ep", qn, default="fallback")
        assert result == "custom-3.0.0"

    def test_qualified_name_fallback_to_default(self) -> None:
        """If the qualified name scheme returns None, the default is used."""
        def returns_none(version: ScmVersion) -> None:
            return None

        # Temporarily inject a function that returns None
        mod = sys.modules[__name__]
        old = getattr(mod, "_returns_none", None)
        mod._returns_none = returns_none  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        try:
            qn = f"{__name__}:_returns_none"
            ver = DummyVersion("4.0.0")
            result = _call_version_scheme(ver, "test_ep", qn, default="fallback")
            assert result == "fallback"
        finally:
            if old is None:
                del mod._returns_none  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
            else:
                mod._returns_none = old

    def test_qualified_name_fallback_to_entry_point(self) -> None:
        """When the qualified name cannot be loaded, the entry point is used."""
        # Use a non‑existent qualified name, then fall back to a known entry
        # point.  The string "guess-next-dev" is not a qualified name (no colon)
        # so it will be treated as an entry point name.
        ver = DummyVersion("5.0.0")
        result = _call_version_scheme(ver, "setuptools_scm.version_scheme", "guess-next-dev", default="fallback")
        # The built‑in scheme should return something like "5.0.0.dev0"
        assert result is not None
        assert "5.0.0" in result


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Integration test: using a qualified name that points to a function defined
# in a temporary module (simulates a real‑world scenario)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_qualified_name_in_temporary_module() -> None:
    """A qualified name pointing to a function in a dynamically created module
    is resolved correctly."""
    # Create a temporary module
    tmp_mod = types.ModuleType("_test_tmp_scheme_mod")
    def tmp_scheme(version: ScmVersion) -> str:
        return f"tmp-{version.tag}"
    tmp_mod.tmp_scheme = tmp_scheme
    sys.modules["_test_tmp_scheme_mod"] = tmp_mod

    try:
        qn = "_test_tmp_scheme_mod:tmp_scheme"
        ver = DummyVersion("6.0.0")
        result = _call_version_scheme(ver, "test_ep", qn, default="fallback")
        assert result == "tmp-6.0.0"
    finally:
        del sys.modules["_test_tmp_scheme_mod"]

import pytest
from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


class TestSyllableTokenizerPerformance:
    """Tests that the SyllableTokenizer does not mutate its internal `vowels`
    attribute when processing unknown characters (e.g., digits), which was the
    root cause of the O(n²) performance regression reported in the issue."""

    def test_vowels_not_mutated_by_numbers(self):
        tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
        initial_vowels = tokenizer.vowels
        result = tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        assert tokenizer.vowels == initial_vowels, (
            "self.vowels should not be mutated after tokenizing a number"
        )
        # Digits are treated as vowels (max sonority), so the whole string
        # should be returned as a single syllable.
        assert result == ["99"]

    def test_vowels_not_mutated_by_mixed_token(self):
        tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
        initial_vowels = tokenizer.vowels
        result = tokenizer.tokenize("a1b2c3")
        assert tokenizer.vowels == initial_vowels
        # The tokenization should succeed without error; exact syllables
        # are not critical for this test.
        assert isinstance(result, list)

    def test_vowels_not_mutated_by_punctuation(self):
        tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
        initial_vowels = tokenizer.vowels
        result = tokenizer.tokenize("hello!")
        assert tokenizer.vowels == initial_vowels
        # Tokenization should succeed; exact output may vary.
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert len(result) > 0

    def test_normal_word_still_works(self):
        tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
        result = tokenizer.tokenize("justification")
        assert result == ["jus", "ti", "fi", "ca", "tion"]

    def test_repeated_tokenization_does_not_change_vowels(self):
        tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
        initial_vowels = tokenizer.vowels
        for _ in range(10):
            tokenizer.tokenize("99")
            tokenizer.tokenize("hello")
        assert tokenizer.vowels == initial_vowels, (
            "Repeated tokenization of numbers and words should not mutate vowels"
        )

    def test_long_number_string_does_not_mutate_vowels(self):
        tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
        initial_vowels = tokenizer.vowels
        long_number = "1234567890" * 100  # 1000 digits
        result = tokenizer.tokenize(long_number)
        assert tokenizer.vowels == initial_vowels
        # The whole string should be one syllable because all digits are
        # treated as vowels.

            title=title,

        if isinstance(result, bytes):

        return result

import warnings
import pytest
from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


class TestSyllableTokenizerPerformance:
    """Tests for the performance fix of SyllableTokenizer on numeric strings."""

    def setup_method(self):
        self.tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    def test_vowels_not_growing_on_numbers(self):
        """Ensure self.vowels does not grow after tokenizing numbers repeatedly."""
        initial_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == initial_vowels, (
            "self.vowels should not grow after tokenizing numbers"
        )

    def test_vowels_not_growing_on_mixed_input(self):
        """Ensure self.vowels does not grow after tokenizing mixed alphanumeric."""
        initial_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("hello123world")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == initial_vowels, (
            "self.vowels should not grow after tokenizing mixed input"
        )

    def test_vowels_not_growing_on_special_chars(self):
        """Ensure self.vowels does not grow after tokenizing special characters."""
        initial_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("@#$%")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == initial_vowels, (
            "self.vowels should not grow after tokenizing special characters"
        )

    def test_numeric_tokenization_single_syllable(self):
        """Numbers should be tokenized as a single syllable (all vowels)."""
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("12345") == ["12345"]
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("0") == ["0"]

    def test_mixed_alphanumeric_tokenization(self):
        """Mixed letters and numbers should be tokenized correctly."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("hello123world")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert len(result) > 0
        assert "".join(result) == "hello123world"

    def test_uppercase_unknown_characters(self):
        """Uppercase letters are not in default phoneme map, treated as vowels."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("ABC")
        assert result == ["ABC"]

    def test_punctuation_only(self):
        """Punctuation-only input should be returned as a single token (no vowels)."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize(".,!?")
        assert result == [".,!?"]

    def test_empty_string(self):
        """Empty string should return a list with an empty string."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("")
        assert result == [""]

    def test_special_characters_warning(self):
        """Non-punctuation unknown characters should produce a warning."""
        with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
            warnings.simplefilter("always")
            # Use a character that is not in punctuation and not in phoneme_map
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("©©©")
            assert len(w) == 3  # three unknown characters
            for warning in w:
                assert "Character not defined in sonority_hierarchy" in str(warning.message)

    def test_word_tokenization_unchanged(self):
        """Standard word tokenization should still work as before."""
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("justification") == [
            "jus",
            "ti",
            "fi",
            "ca",
            "tion",
        ]
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("hello") == ["hel", "lo"]
        assert self.tokenizer.tokenize("world") == ["world"]

    def test_repeated_calls_no_performance_degradation(self):
        """Many calls with numbers should not degrade performance (vowels length constant)."""
        initial_vowels_len = len(self.tokenizer.vowels)
        for _ in range(1000):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        assert len(self.tokenizer.vowels) == initial_vowels_len

    def test_long_numeric_string(self):
        """Very long numeric string should be tokenized as a single syllable."""
        long_num = "9" * 100
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize(long_num)
        assert result == [long_num]

    def test_mixed_case_and_numbers(self):
        """Mixed case and numbers should be handled."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("ABC999xyz")
        assert "".join(result) == "ABC999xyz"

    def test_tokenize_with_custom_hierarchy(self):
        """Custom sonority hierarchy should still work."""
        custom = SyllableTokenizer(
            sonority_hierarchy=["aeiou", "bcdfg", "hklmnp"]
        )
        result = custom.tokenize("abc")
        assert "".join(result) == "abc"

        for i, arg in enumerate(args):

        # Check that there is an argument starting with --title=
        title_args = [arg for arg in args if str(arg).startswith("--title=")]
        self.assertEqual(len(title_args), 1, "Expected exactly one --title= argument")
