    def test_mpv_title_uses_equals(self):
        """mpv title argument must use --title=value format."""
        po = PlayerOutput(
            cmd="/usr/bin/mpv",
            args="-",
            title="Test Title"
        )
        args = po._create_arguments()
        # args is a list on POSIX
        self.assertIn("--title=Test Title", args)
        # Ensure there is no separate "--title" followed by "Test Title"
        self.assertNotIn("--title", args)  # because "--title" would be a separate element

    def test_mpv_title_with_spaces(self):
        """Title with spaces should be properly quoted in the equals format."""
        po = PlayerOutput(
            cmd="/usr/bin/mpv",
            args="-",
            title="My Stream Title"
        )
        args = po._create_arguments()
        self.assertIn("--title=My Stream Title", args)

    def test_mpv_title_with_special_chars(self):
        """Title with special characters should be escaped and use equals."""
        po = PlayerOutput(
            cmd="/usr/bin/mpv",
            args="-",
            title="Stream $pecial"
        )
        args = po._create_arguments()
        # The title is escaped: $ becomes $$
        self.assertIn("--title=Stream $$pecial", args)

    def test_mpv_title_empty(self):
        """Empty title should still use equals format."""
        po = PlayerOutput(
            cmd="/usr/bin/mpv",
            args="-",
            title=""
        )
        args = po._create_arguments()
        self.assertIn("--title=", args)

            args="-",
            title="Test Title"
        )
        args = po._create_arguments()
        # VLC should have separate "--input-title-format" and "Test Title"
        idx = args.index("--input-title-format")
        self.assertEqual(args[idx + 1], "Test Title")

import time
import warnings

import pytest
from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


class TestSyllableTokenizerPerformance:
    """Tests for the SyllableTokenizer performance fix (issue #...)."""

    def setup_method(self):
        self.tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    def test_vowels_not_modified_by_digits(self):
        """Tokenizing digits must not extend the vowels string."""
        initial_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels
        long_digits = "9" * 1000
        self.tokenizer.tokenize(long_digits)
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == initial_vowels

    def test_vowels_not_modified_by_mixed_unknown(self):
        """Tokenizing many different unknown characters must not extend vowels."""
        initial_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels
        # Use a range of non-ASCII characters that are not in the hierarchy
        unknown = "".join(chr(i) for i in range(1000, 1100))
        self.tokenizer.tokenize(unknown)
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == initial_vowels

    def test_tokenize_numbers_returns_list(self):
        """Tokenizing numbers should return a list of strings (no crash)."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert all(isinstance(s, str) for s in result)

    def test_tokenize_long_digit_string_fast(self):
        """Tokenizing a long digit string must not exhibit O(n²) slowdown."""
        long_digits = "9" * 1000
        # Warm up
        self.tokenizer.tokenize(long_digits)
        # Timed run
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize(long_digits)
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
        # With the fix this should be well under 1 second; set a generous limit.
        assert elapsed < 5.0, f"Tokenizing 1000 digits 100 times took {elapsed:.3f}s"

    def test_tokenize_word_still_works(self):
        """Normal word tokenization must remain correct."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("justification")
        assert result == ["jus", "ti", "fi", "ca", "tion"]

    def test_tokenize_mixed_numbers_and_letters(self):
        """Mixed input should not cause errors or state corruption."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("abc123def")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert all(isinstance(s, str) for s in result)

    def test_warning_on_unknown_char(self):
        """Unknown non-punctuation characters should still produce a warning."""
        with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
            warnings.simplefilter("always")
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("9")  # digit is not punctuation, triggers warning
            assert len(w) == 1
            assert "Character not defined" in str(w[0].message)

import pytest
from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


class TestSyllableTokenizerPerformance:
    """Tests for the SyllableTokenizer performance fix (issue #???)."""

    def setup_method(self):
        self.tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
        self.original_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels

    def test_vowels_not_growing_after_numeric_calls(self):
        """Repeated tokenization of numbers must not enlarge self.vowels."""
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == self.original_vowels, (
            f"vowels grew from {self.original_vowels!r} to {self.tokenizer.vowels!r}"
        )

    def test_vowels_not_growing_after_mixed_unknown_chars(self):
        """Repeated tokenization of various unknown characters must not enlarge self.vowels."""
        for _ in range(50):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("123abc!@#")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == self.original_vowels

    def test_vowels_not_growing_after_long_numeric_string(self):
        """Tokenizing a long numeric string once must not enlarge self.vowels."""
        self.tokenizer.tokenize("12345678901234567890")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == self.original_vowels

    def test_numeric_tokenization_returns_single_syllable(self):
        """Numbers should be treated as vowels and form a single syllable."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        assert result == ["99"], f"Expected ['99'], got {result}"

    def test_mixed_tokenization_preserves_vowels(self):
        """Tokenizing mixed content must not modify self.vowels."""
        self.tokenizer.tokenize("abc123def")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == self.original_vowels

    def test_known_word_tokenization_still_works(self):
        """Existing word tokenization must remain correct."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("justification")
        assert result == ["jus", "ti", "fi", "ca", "tion"]

    def test_empty_string(self):
        """Empty string should not cause errors or modify vowels."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == self.original_vowels

    def test_punctuation_only(self):
        """Punctuation-only input should not modify vowels."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize(".,!?")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == self.original_vowels

    def test_special_characters(self):
        """Special characters (e.g., @, #, $) should not modify vowels."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("@#$%")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == self.original_vowels

    def test_repeated_calls_with_same_unknown_char(self):
        """Repeated calls with the same unknown character must not grow vowels."""
        for _ in range(10):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize("999")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == self.original_vowels

    def test_multiple_different_unknown_chars(self):
        """Using different unknown characters across calls must not grow vowels."""
        for s in ["9", "8", "7", "6", "5"]:
            self.tokenizer.tokenize(s)
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == self.original_vowels

    def test_case_sensitivity(self):
        """Uppercase letters are in phoneme_map, so they should not trigger the warning path."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("ABC999xyz")
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == self.original_vowels

    def test_vowels_unchanged_after_multiple_calls_with_different_inputs(self):
        """A sequence of different inputs must not change vowels."""
        inputs = ["hello", "99", "world", "123", "test", "!@#", "abc123def"]
        for inp in inputs:
            self.tokenizer.tokenize(inp)
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == self.original_vowels

import time
from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


class TestSyllableTokenizerPerformance:
    """Tests for the sonority sequencing syllable tokenizer performance fix.

    The issue reported that tokenizing numbers was O(n^2) while tokenizing
    words was O(n). The fix ensures that unknown characters (like digits) are
    not added to the internal `vowels` attribute, which was causing the
    quadratic slowdown due to regex pattern growth in `validate_syllables`.
    """

    def setup_method(self):
        self.tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    def test_tokenize_number_returns_single_syllable(self):
        """Tokenizing a number should return the whole token as one syllable."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        assert result == ["99"]

    def test_tokenize_long_number_returns_single_syllable(self):
        """Tokenizing a long number should still return a single syllable."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("1234567890")
        assert result == ["1234567890"]

    def test_tokenize_word_returns_correct_syllables(self):
        """Tokenizing a word should return correct syllables (SSP)."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("justification")
        assert result == ["jus", "ti", "fi", "ca", "tion"]

    def test_vowels_not_modified_by_numbers(self):
        """After tokenizing numbers, the vowels attribute should be unchanged."""
        original_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels
        self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        self.tokenizer.tokenize("12345")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

    def test_vowels_not_modified_by_mixed_input(self):
        """After tokenizing mixed letters and digits, vowels should be unchanged."""
        original_vowels = self.tokenizer.vowels
        self.tokenizer.tokenize("a1b2c3")
        assert self.tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

    def test_tokenize_mixed_letters_and_digits(self):
        """Tokenizing a mix of letters and digits should not raise errors."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("a1b2c3")
        # The tokenizer should return a list of strings (syllables).
        assert isinstance(result, list)
        assert all(isinstance(s, str) for s in result)

    def test_tokenize_punctuation(self):
        """Tokenizing punctuation should assign -1 and break syllables."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("hello.world")
        # Punctuation '.' should cause a syllable break.
        assert "." in result

    def test_tokenize_long_number_performance(self):
        """Tokenizing a long number should be roughly as fast as a long word.

        This test verifies that the O(n^2) behavior is fixed. We compare the
        time to tokenize a long digit string vs a long word string of similar
        length. The digit tokenization should not be dramatically slower.
        """
        long_number = "9" * 1000
        long_word = "a" * 1000  # all vowels, so early return

        # Warm up
        self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        self.tokenizer.tokenize("aa")

        # Time tokenizing the long number
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize(long_number)
        number_time = time.perf_counter() - start

        # Time tokenizing the long word
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(100):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize(long_word)
        word_time = time.perf_counter() - start

        # The number tokenization should not be more than 10x slower than the word.
        # (In practice, with the fix, they should be comparable; the factor 10
        #  is a generous safety margin to avoid flakiness.)
        assert number_time < 10 * word_time, (
            f"Tokenizing numbers is too slow: {number_time:.4f}s vs {word_time:.4f}s"
        )

    def test_tokenize_long_number_linear_time(self):
        """Tokenizing numbers of increasing length should show linear time.

        This test checks that the time grows roughly linearly, not quadratically.
        We tokenize strings of length N and 2N, and verify that the time ratio
        is not close to 4 (which would indicate O(n^2)).
        """
        # Use lengths that are large enough to expose quadratic behavior
        n = 500
        short_number = "9" * n
        long_number = "9" * (2 * n)

        # Warm up
        self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")

        # Time short number
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(50):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize(short_number)
        short_time = time.perf_counter() - start

        # Time long number
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(50):
            self.tokenizer.tokenize(long_number)
        long_time = time.perf_counter() - start

        # If O(n^2), doubling length would quadruple time (ratio ~4).
        # If O(n), ratio should be ~2. Allow some overhead.
        ratio = long_time / short_time if short_time > 0 else float("inf")
        assert ratio < 3.5, (
            f"Time ratio {ratio:.2f} suggests quadratic behavior; "
            f"short={short_time:.4f}s, long={long_time:.4f}s"
        )

    def test_tokenize_word_still_works_after_numbers(self):
        """Tokenizing words after numbers should still produce correct syllables."""
        self.tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        self.tokenizer.tokenize("12345")
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("justification")
        assert result == ["jus", "ti", "fi", "ca", "tion"]

    def test_tokenize_empty_string(self):
        """Tokenizing an empty string should return a list with an empty string."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("")
        assert result == [""]

    def test_tokenize_single_character(self):
        """Tokenizing a single character should return it as a single syllable."""
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("a")
        assert result == ["a"]
        result = self.tokenizer.tokenize("9")
        assert result == ["9"]
